Now, fast forward to today; The Carnivore compliments the heritage of Edinburgh’s meat market and this is where our ethos of great quality meat for unbeatable value was born. The fuss-free food features authentic meat-lover’s classics with a twist, paired with American-inspired whiskey cocktail. Free Fringe comedy every day during August Fringe.

Title: Call Me Blondie
Description: Call Me Blondie are a Southampton-based Blondie tribute act with one of the most accomplished and experienced line-ups working on the tribute circuit today. The Call me Blondie act covers everything from early punk classics such as X-Offender, right through to crowd-pleasing hits like The Tide is High. Across two 40-minute sets of punk/pop excellence Call Me Blondie will make this show one to remember.
Venue: The A Club at the Merchants Hall
Venue description: A visit to The A Club is an amazing experience, an occasion to enjoy a fantastic mix of live music shows, stunning Arbikie cocktails and table-service food. Throughout August you can relax and unwind whilst enjoying some of the world’s top shows of pop, jazz, folk and rock music. In the heart of Edinburgh, The Merchants’ Hall is just off Princes Street and walking distance from Waverley Railway Station.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Wild and Majestic: Romantic Visions of Scotland
Description: Dramatic Highland landscapes, heroic histories, tartan and bagpipes are among the defining images of Scotland for many people around the world today. From the Romantic movement of the 18th and early 19th centuries to Queen Victoria’s Highland idyll at Balmoral, consider the origins of these ideas and explore how they were used to represent Scotland around the world. Featuring rich displays and iconic objects, this landmark exhibition charts Scotland’s journey into the global imagination and invites you to think again about the meaning and relevance of ideas that continue to define Scotland today.
Venue description: Explore the diversity of the natural world, world cultures, art and design, science and technology, and Scottish history, all under one roof at the National Museum of Scotland.

Title: Monster Gay
Description: I’m back with a new show delving into all the things I hate about myself, in under an hour! From my ‘gay voice’ to my fat arse; I’m learning how scary it can be to love yourself. Are you brave enough to join me? 'Audience in stitches' (Sun). 'Dixon has a remarkable gift' (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Hauntingly beautiful' (No one).
Artist: Martin J Dixon / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue: PBH's Free Fringe @ The Outhouse Bar
Venue description: The St Andrews Brewing Co have recently taken over the Outhouse, so expect a few improvements to this Edinburgh institution. Located just off Broughton Street this popular bar also has a beer garden open during the summer months serving BBQ foods. The bar has a lively atmosphere with family friendly crowds during the day and party goers late evenings. During August PBH Free Fringe will be providing free shows everyday.

Title: World Press Photo Exhibition
Description: This exhibition showcases a collection of award-winning press photography. It will feature almost 150 of the most compelling and powerful examples of photojournalism taken over the course of 2018 from all over the world. The moving images depict stories from a range of categories including general news, the environment, sports and nature.
Venue description: The Scottish Parliament building
Venue accessibility: The event taking place at the Parliament is a photography exhibition which will be captioned. There will also be information available on request. Title: Don't Do It, Don't Do It, Do It!
Description: Do it or don't do it? Do it, obviously! Join the award-winning Gaulier and Pochinko-trained clown and her singing vagina on an odyssey of sexual catastrophe. A one-woman dynamo, feminist, physical comedy character-filled epic from the UK and Canada, with puppetry, mask and music.  **** 'Full of humour and poignancy, there is never a dull moment... For a show you’ll still be talking about days later, this is the one to see!' (TheUpsideNews.com). Award-winning one-of-a-kind clown delivers a uniquely eccentric show, unlike anything you've seen before' (WeekendNotes.co.uk).
Warnings: Audience Participation, Contains Distressing Themes, Scenes of a Sexual Nature, Strobe Lighting
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival. Stylish well stocked on-site bars give audiences the ultimate sense of occasion and comfort so rare on the fringe.

Title: Queer Faith and TheMany – Radical Faeries
Description: This show invites you to come and sit or stand together with others, co-creating a safe and inclusive space for us all to relax in. React or stay quiet, cry or laugh, meet again with our inner faerie(s). A genderqueer blue collection of creatures in one body will bring past stories back through this surreal, immersive and intimate story-singing show celebrating emotions related to love, multiplicity and emotional nakednesss...

Title: Everybody Be Cool, This Is a Comedy
Description: The comedy heist of the year! Hot off the London circuit, Will Preston (South Coast Comedian of the Year semi-finalist) and Ben Peel (So You Think You're Funny? semi-finalist and shortlisted for BBC New Comedy Award) take the stage hostage with off-the-wall/chain/hook comedy and profound social commentary. Come in for lots of laughs and leave with your life intact. And remember – Everybody Be Cool, This Is a Comedy!
Artist: Will Preston and Ben Peel / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A friendly neighbourhood bar with a great choice of craft, cask beers, wines and spirits, friendly staff and a delicious new menu. Last orders during Fringe: 3am. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our function room from 12noon-midnight.

Title: Gynie Hub
Description: Calling all those who possess a uterus, including trans men, at the Fringe! How's our centre of creativity; the womb and ovaries being compromised within a demanding product driven system? Come share a cuppa and chat in a relaxed space about your gynae health. Maybe you're going through the menopause, have troublesome periods, hormonal problems or polycystic ovaries? Or maybe you don’t know what the hell these things are and you want to find out more. This is a safe space for those working within the creative industries to share personal experiences, swap tips and ask for help.
Venue description: Fringe Central is a resource developed specifically for Fringe participants. A hub for professional and creative development opportunities and home to our Arts Industry, Media and Venues and Companies offices, you will find support and advice as well as a programme of over 100 free events all designed to help you make the most out of your Fringe experience.

Title: Mary Houlihan: Me and Jack
Description: Comedian Mary Houlihan tells the true (fake) story of her torrid romance with 82-year-old actor Jack Nicholson. Joke-packed storytelling, musical numbers, visual aids and a giant talking Jack Nicholson head. Think A Star Is Born, but dumb (in a good way). Mary has been lauded by Vulture, Forbes and Entertainment Weekly, and was named the 'best of what’s next' by Paste Magazine, and a 'comedian we love' by Time Out. She has written for The New Yorker and McSweeney’s and appeared on Broad City, Difficult People, The Chris Gethard Show, Jimmy Kimmel Live and more.
Venue: PBH's Free Fringe @ Bar Bados Complex
Venue description: Seven-plus stages and two bars (Cowshed Bar and Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH's Free Fringe shows and music everyday (comedy, spoken word, theatre, cabaret, live music). During the month of August this venue transforms into a Free Fringe multi-stage complex with an unrivaled choice of free comedy shows and live music.

Title: The Voice of Young China
Description: The Youth Choir of Shanghai Grand Theatre present a delightful programme of classical and popular material. East and West come together in this joyous celebration of youth and the power of music.
Artist: Youth Choir of Shanghai Grand Theatre / Asian Arts Global
Venue description: Lauriston Halls (both modernised) are situated between the Grassmarket and Tollcross, 10 minutes walk from Princes Street. The Large Hall has air conditioning and a sprung floor. It is a regular ceilidh (Scottish dance) venue popular with locals and visitors.

Title: Elliot Steel: Merked
Description: Elliot has done a sober stint, completed a Roast Battle with his dad and got merked in a Muay Thai fight. This is as good as toxic masculinity gets. As seen on Comedy Central’s Roast Battle, Live From The Comedy Store and BBC's The Premier League Show. 'Brilliantly detailed snapshots of adolescent life... great gags' (Guardian).
Artist: Off the Kerb Productions / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Bannermans is one of Edinburgh's premier live music venues, located in the heart of the historic Old Town. A proven firm favorite with locals and tourists for many years now. Open from 12:00-01:00 every day, apart from Sundays when we open at 12:30. No under 18s. www.bannermanslive.co.uk
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, No reserved accessible parking. Entrance to the venue is fully level, however there is a single step into the toilets

Description: An unstable space without an exit. Three female prisoners, bound by their own original sins, yearn to be redeemed. K, with her chastity and faith; S, with her childhood father's shadow; M, with her unacknowledged love. They are both individuals and united. In this space without form, they defend themselves still eager for love, however hopelessness and fear of death surrounds them as a cloud of smoke fills the silence after lights out.
Artist: Goldsmiths Chinese Traditional Theatre Art Society
Venue description: Greenside @ Nicolson Square is set in the heart of town, seconds from the Festival Theatre, the flashing lights of Bristo Square and the hustle and bustle of the Royal Mile. We’re bringing our desire for creating great spaces and passion for service to the heart of the festival.

Title: Soup Group!
Description: Two chefs are meant to be making a soup. But they keep getting distracted and the only thing they stir up is a lot of chaos. Silly physical comedy for all the family from Phil O'Shea ('utter, delicious nonsense' (Fest)) and James McIntosh ('The next Ross Noble' (Skinny)).
Venue description: Monkey Barrel Comedy is on Blair Steet in Edinburgh's Old Town, bringing you the best acts in the best rooms at this year's Fringe.
Venue accessibility: WA and WC only for Monkey Barrel 1. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Goodbye Mr President
Description: Goodbye Mr President. President Obonjo, is an up-and-coming, and increasingly successful, stand-up comedian. As the uber-confident, self-appointed dictator of Lafta Republic, he has been leading a covert comedy revolution to become the first President to take the UK comedy industry by storm. This, his third Edinburgh show, is a short, impactful story of friendship between an African dictator and an Englishman. 'President Obonjo has everything you’d expect of a tinpot African dictator… a great comic construct' (Chortle.co.uk). 'A fascinating, bewildering and painfully funny experience' (FringeGuru.com). Hilarious hour in the company of an African dictator.
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award-winning entertainment venue with a cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860's interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The Speakeasy, Ballroom and Space 3 will be used during the festival by some of the best PBH's Free Fringe performers on the cabaret and comedy circuit.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Getting Better
Description: An uplifting solo performance of one man's struggle with PTSD and depression and his journey to well-being. Ex-serviceman Trace Dann shares how he loses his successful corporate career and music business falling into a pit from which there seems no escape.  Anger, outbursts, paranoia, mistrust and failing self-worth see relationships crumble until he breaks mentally and physically.  We then join him as he seeks professional support and takes a, not always easy, road to recovery.  With a personal soundtrack this show is perfect for families, friends and sufferers of depression, anxiety and PTSD.
Warnings:
Simulated anger and discussion of suicide.
Strong Language/Swearing, Other
Venue description: Very central, relaxing bar and performer friendly.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Cold Blooded Witch: The Sex Musical!
Description: Maggie Lalley's one-woman musical comedy tells the true story of her demented stint as a teen witch. Maggie manages to turn this dark tale of cultish charm, magical cunnilingus and the conjuring of Rupert Grint's warlock penis into an unforgettably hilarious musical. Voted Best Musical Comedy in Solocom Festival NYC 2018! Multiple sold-out runs at UCB, Magnet and People's Improv Theater in New York! Voted one of the Best One Woman Shows to See by Time Out NY!
Venue description: The modern Festival's smartest multi-space destination venue. The ultimate powerhouse of live performance offering a pulsating programme of diverse performance. Part of our 10-space hub at the very stylish Surgeons Hall. Featuring the Festival's largest programme of new writing, theatre, musicals, children's shows, sketch, improv, acapella, dance, physical, spoken word, poetry and comedy. Stylish, well-stocked bars and great food make this the perfect destination for audiences to spend a day.

Title: Evers, Booth and [Name]
Description: Evers, Booth and [Name] courageously stage their 2019 multimedia sketch show. Despite the unfortunate disappearance of their third member, Evers and Booth must fulfil their contractual obligations to Eastern European sponsor Mmm, Dank! (3-in-1 carpet cleaner, antifreeze and feminine moist wipe). Among those helping them are: un-electronic Amish house band Bounty of Beards, hula-hooping dominatrix Barbara and Yorkshire-based Yankophile, T-bone. Not forgetting Katerina, the miserable face of Mmm, Dank! 'Finely written sketches with lo-fi elements and double entendres galore... Masters of the most unlikely combinations' (List).

Title: Blake Freeman and Dan Rath – Far From Home
Description: After sell-out shows and scooping up awards at Melbourne and Sydney comedy festivals, Blake and Dan are setting off to Edinburgh to take part in the world's biggest arts festival! Nervous but excited, one thing's for sure these boys are far from home. Blake Freeman, Best Newcomer 2019 Melbourne International Comedy Festival. 'Live, direct and has the easy, candid demeanour of a man born to be a comedian' ****½ (Herald Sun). Dan Rath, Best Newcomer 2019 Melbourne International Comedy Festival nominee. 'Wildly creative ideas and entertainingly idiosyncratic jokes' (Chortle.co.uk).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Grassmarket Centre
Venue description: A very modern large space attached to an old kirk building. Centrally located where Grassmarket meets Cowgate. An outside bar, full cafe facilities and the expertise of Just the Tonic. The most exciting new space on the Fringe.

Title: Gill Sims: Why Mummy Doesn’t Give A ****!
Description: Author of online sensation Peter and Jane, Gill Sims is the number one best-selling author behind Why Mummy Drinks, its follow up "Why Mummy Swears and the recently announced Why Mummy Doesn't Give A... Join Gill as she is interviewed about her blog, books, character and much more! There will be readings from her books and also a chance to ask Gill questions from the audience. Books will be available to purchase and sign as well.
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in 17 venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman). Open until 03:00.

Title: The Living Room
Description: These Accountants of Death work tirelessly to record the death toll. The occupational hazards wear on these two clowns as they learn the meaning of life and death. An absurd and physical jaunt brimming with existential phone calls, impaired dancing and the love of a goldfish. The Living Room rides the very fine line between comedy and tragedy. Employing physical and absurdist theatre techniques, this show leaves the audience laughing and crying and thrust out into the night to ponder it all.
Venue description: This classic building in the heart of the New Town is now the centre of a fantastic Festival hub which is host to some of the finest theatre, comedy and music from around the world. The Assembly Rooms hosts three spaces indoors: the Music Hall, Ballroom and Drawing Room, with a Spiegeltent (The Bijou) and two studio spaces (Front Room and Powder Room) outside on George Street.

Title: Only Bones 1.0 – Thom Monckton
Description: On a tiny set lit by a single bulb, endless possibilities are illuminated. Wordlessly using body manipulation, dance, circus and clownery, Only Bones' quirky low- tech aesthetic strips the stage down to one performer, one technician, one light, no text and a stage area of little more than 1m2. With head juggling and jellyfish this is a hypnotic show about a lot, using very little. NZ Fringe award winner in physical theatre, 2015. ‘A glorious salute to one man's remarkable physicality’ ***** (Herald). ‘Mind-blowing’ ***** (AcrosstheArts.co.uk). ‘...extraordinary inventiveness created by a limitless imagination’ (Theatreview.org.nz).
Artist: Kallo Collective in association with Aurora Nova

Title: Richard Wright Is Just Happy to be Involved
Description: Richard Wright is just happy to be involved. He loves the Edinburgh Fringe. It's the most wonderful time of the year. He loves it so much he lost out on a job to come do this. Why did he do that? That's not the point. He's here and much like Robbie Williams he just wants to entertain you. For like an hour. Max.
Venue description: Opium alternative bar and nightclub is Edinburgh's longest running dedicated rock venue. Open seven days a week until 5am, Opium offers the very best in alternative entertainment. Title: Time Flies
Description: Join farmers David and Sam, as they share with you their untold adventures, full of mishaps and misfortunes. Unfortunately they can't promise facts. They can't even promise to make it to the end of the show. But they can promise an anarchic kaleidoscope of physical comedy, mediocre magic and a love story with a cow. Complete with a disco soundtrack, David and Sam are sure to put a smile on everyone's face! 'Time Flies is a bit like War Horse but with a cow' (Rich Rusk, Associate Director for Gecko Theatre).

Title: The Slinks
Description: A melodramatic poet, a curious clown and a slanted piano. Join The Slinks, two Freedom Hunters in their late night kooky, glamorous world of music and comedy. A show steeped in satin and emotional warfare. Multi-disciplinary two-piece, Lily Ashley and Hugo Hamlet use their impish talent in a surprising and off-piste premier. Follow this eccentric double act through song, dance, piano, poetry, clown, oboe, costumes and mime as they translate the absurdity of a performer's life.

Title: Summer School Showcase – A Musical Medley
Description: Experience a slice of West End in Edinburgh, with a musical theatre showcase presented by Goldsmiths, University of London's Musical Theatre Summer School students! Featuring new and emerging talent from Asia, this showcase features a variety of beloved and showstopping musical theatre pieces presented by talented enthusiasts. As a culmination of all their hard work over the intensive two-week summer school in London, this showcase aims to give them the stage to shine. Be a part of these aspiring musical theatre enthusiasts' unforgettable summer school experience by joining them for this thrilling finale!
Artist: Goldsmiths Musical Theatre Summer School 2019 Cohort
Venue description: Royal Terrace is special. It is a hidden gem – it’s 'one of the most charming venues at the Fringe' so Lyn Gardner said and we like to think it is too.

Title: Sarawak: Mystical Chants of the Rainforest
Description: Connect with the indigenous culture of Sarawak on the island of Borneo through the chants of the weaver calling down the spirits, and the traditional music inspired by the nature of the rainforest before enjoying some food for a taste of Sarawak.
Warnings:
There is an end-of-show Jungle Cry and the audience will be encouraged. Those participating in the final jungle dance will get a taste of snacks being served and a shot of rice wine.
Audience Participation, Other

Title: Triplex Adventures
Description: A spoiled boy, Chao, decides to run away from the world of chocolates, ice cream, fries and decayed teeth to a new healthy world. However, these villains won’t give up without putting up a good fight. Meanwhile, Chao also meets his new friends: alarm clock, water, vegetables and sporty shoes. Most importantly, he is learning how to resist all the temptations. Winner of the Gold Award at Beijing Student Art Festival, Blue Bird's young performers present an exciting musical showcase of devised stories of Change Myself, An Adventure in Teeth Street and a youth version of Hakuna Matata.

Title: A Complicated Man
Description: How many years does it take to unspool a man? An odd king sails the waves of the wine dark sea in a bathtub. Featuring water and wigs, big mammal reimagines The Odyssey as a queer epic of becoming. This new work by Emma Henry and Evan Silver refigures the Homeric text to explore the fluidity of gender and the multiplicity of identity. Developed at Bussey Building's CLF Art Cafe in Peckham, London.

Title: Split the Bill – Claire Haus, Suzie Preece and Josh Weller
Description: Three 30-somethings. One hour of stand-up. Full mental collapse. Josh Weller: ‘My favourite new favourite comedian’ (Alfie Brown). 'Look out for Josh Weller, he's on the path to greatness. The jokes and stage prowess of someone who's been going for ten years' (Sara Barron). Claire Haus: 'If this woman isn't a breakthrough act this festival, I will punch God' (Logan Murray). 'This is a very funny lady' (Shappi Khorsandi). Suzie Preece: 'A stand out' (Kate Maltby, Times).
Artist: Claire Haus, Suzie Preece and Josh Weller
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms of free Fringe shows every day from 10:00 to 02:30. There's a massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, food and drink plus a restaurant downstairs. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking

Title: Qi
Description: Qi, a syllable coming from the performance maker’s name, is believed to be the life force of any living entity in traditional Chinese philosophy (sometimes also spelt as Chi). The movement-based performance is inspired by the meanings and shapes of pictographic characters. By looking at the connection between rough materials, body, sound, space and self awareness, a multi-sensory experience will be offered.
Venue description: The Old Dr Bells Baths has been re-invented. So why not have your event at Edinburgh’s brand new venue? Built in the Victorian era, The Old Dr Bells Baths is a much loved listed building located in the heart of Leith, 121 Great Junction Street. Now the renovated site is open as a multi-purpose venue hosting a range of events including weddings, live music events, office parties and many more.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. All areas very easily accessible

Title: The Sustainability Hub
Description: New this year, the Festival Sustainability Hub is dedicated to supporting sustainability and the community throughout the Festival Fringe. The Hub is coordinated by the University of Edinburgh’s Department for Social Responsibility and Sustainability, who will be hosting events throughout the Festival. The rest of the time will be split between participant support, sustainable shopping options and events hosted by local community groups, all working to benefit the community and improve the sustainability of the Festival! For more information and a full Hub schedule, check out www.edin.ac/festival.
Artist: The University of Edinburgh Department for Social Responsibility and Sustainability
Venue description: The Bayes Centre is the University of Edinburgh’s Data-Driven Innovation Hub and the Courtyard is an outside space shared with the Design Informatics studio, Informatics Forum and the University of Edinburgh Visitor Centre.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Dead Ringers Live
Description: The legendary BBC Radio 4 series hits the Edinburgh Fringe for the first time in this special live residency starring the dream team of Jon Culshaw, Jan Ravens, Lewis MacLeod and Duncan Wisbey. Featuring a mixture of classic sketches, new martial and of course, the trademark sharp, topical humour for which Dead Ringers has won critical acclaim over its nearly 20-year history. ‘Gorgeously funny’ **** (Times).
Artist: So Comedy and Broken Robot Productions, by arrangement with BBC
Venue description: Join us in the heart of Edinburgh’s West End for the most spectacular circus, dance, theatre, comedy and much, much more! The best of the Fringe awaits in the city’s most luxurious venue, where brilliant bars and cafés join a stellar line up of world renowned artists.
Venue accessibility: All performance spaces are accessible. Customers with access requirements are encouraged to contact the venue in advance and to make themselves known to a member of the team upon arrival to access lifts. A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The EICC’s two main entrances, the Strathblane and the Lennox, both have automated sliding doors which are operated by a push button from the outside and by sensor from the inside. During an event these doors are manned with security who can offer assistance if required.

Title: Ragazziquintet
Description: The Ragazziquintet is a group of five string musicians from the Netherlands making their Edinburgh Fringe debut at AMC. They have been best friends since they were little kids and have been making music with each other for more than six years. Their repertoire consists of their own arrangements and compositions, with a lot of room for improvisation. In their show they will take you through a variety of genres and styles, while entertaining with their enthusiasm and positive energy. In other words, an evening you won't forget for all the best reasons!
Venue description: The venue is on the ground floor of a classic 200-year-old Georgian townhouse looking north across the Forth from Calton Hill.
Venue accessibility: Royal Terrace is flat and approached up a gradient either from the top of Leith Walk/London Road or Abbeyhill. The basement entrance is accessed by stone steps down from street level. The main entrance to the building has access from a single stone step preceeded by four stone steps up from the pavement. There is a ramp to help wheelchair users enter. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The venue does not have a lift. The basement bar is inaccessible to wheelchairs

Title: 300 to 1
Description: What's better than a glorious death?  Escaping his war poetry homework, 15-year-old Elliot re-enacts the movie 300 to the ghosts of Wilfred Owen and Siegfried Sassoon.  Corin Rhys Jones returns to the Fringe with the award-winning production of this comical and moving one-man show.  Written and directed by Matt Panesh.
Artist: Love and War Theatre / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue: PBH's Free Fringe @ Bar Bados Complex
Venue description: Seven-plus stages and two bars (Cowshed Bar and Bar-Bados) under one roof. PBH's Free Fringe shows and music everyday (comedy, spoken word, theatre, cabaret, live music). During the month of August this venue transforms into a Free Fringe multi-stage complex with an unrivaled choice of free comedy shows and live music.

Title: Sina – The Girl Who Cast Her Shadow
Description: Why does your shadow keep following you? Does it really have to? And what is it up to while you are asleep? Sina finds a way to get rid of her shadow. But living without it is strange. Join her on her journey to get it back, in this fun family-friendly live radio play.
Artist: Donkey for Nights / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue: PBH's Free Fringe @ BrewDog Lothian Rd
Venue description: Located in the old Clydesdale Bank building on Lothian Road Festival Square. During the Edinburgh Fringe we will be providing Free Fringe shows everyday, 25 taps of craft beers, amazing menu, outside seating area.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Wheelchair lift from bar to upper level lounge and function room (The Garage). If not taking the lift there are five steps into the performance space

Title: Spontaneous Sherlock
Description: Returning to Fringe for one night only! Spontaneous Sherlock is an entirely improvised Sherlock Holmes comedy play based on an audience suggestion of a title – with live Victorian musical accompaniment! Performed by the comedy improvisers behind the critically acclaimed and award-winning Spontaneous Potter. 'Unbeatably clever' ***** (EdinburghGuide.com). 'Flawlessly executed improv comedy... pure, unadulterated hilarity' ***** (EdFringeReview.com). Scottish Comedy Award winner (Best Variety). Top 100 Best-Rated Shows, Edinburgh Fringe 2017 (List).
Venue description: Based in the old Charlotte Chapel, Gilded Balloon Rose Theatre has three first-class performance spaces, bars and showcases the very best in comedy, theatre, music and children's shows. Due to the nature and age of the building, none of the performance spaces are wheelchair accessible.
Venue accessibility: For further information about accessibility at Gilded Balloon venues email accessibility@gildedballoon.co.uk. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Due to the historical nature of the building, none of the performance spaces are wheelchair accessible. For more information, please see www.gildedballoon.co.uk/accessibility

Title: Belongings
Description: Missing someone is lonely when you are far away, it's worse when they are right there. We all have a place we can call home but what happens when those closest to you diminish your sense of belonging? Deb is no stranger to conflict on the front-line, but her biggest battle is yet to come as she combats family affairs and reflects upon her time in Afghanistan. Eye2Eye Theatre uses innovative explorations of theatre and television acting to examine the complexities of family, love and moving on in a multimedia production of Morgan Lloyd Malcolm's Belongings.
Warnings: Contains Distressing Themes, Scenes of a Sexual Nature, Scenes of Sexual Violence, Strobe Lighting, Strong Language/Swearing
Venue description: At the foot of the Royal Mile, Venue 13 has been bringing the best of emerging talent from the UK and the wider world to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe since 1996. With a real focus on theatre, but also contemporary dance and physical performance, Venue 13 prides itself on offering more than just simply Fringe theatre. Audiences keep coming back for more to ‘this serene little venue’ (Scotsman).
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The pedestrian route available from the Royal Mile is wheelchair accessible

Title: Darren Connell: Abandon All Hope
Description: Star of Scot Squad, Darren Connell comes to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe for one night only! Nominated for a BAFTA, Darren is best known for portraying the lovable Bobby Muir on BBC Scotland. Dark, twisted and hilarious, prepare to see Darren as you’ve never seen him before. Dry, surreal and stripped-back stand-up comedy. Who knows what issues Connell will raise in his latest show, Abandon All Hope.
Venue description: Monkey Barrel Comedy is on Blair Steet in Edinburgh's Old Town, bringing you the best acts in the best rooms at this year's Fringe.
Venue accessibility: WA and WC only for Monkey Barrel 1. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Newtongrange Silver Band in Concert
Description: Newtongrange Silver Band is a traditional mining village brass band based on the outskirts of Edinburgh, but their repertoire is far from traditional.  Following a successful year so far in several brass band championships and competitions, Newtongrange Silver Band are delighted to return to the Fringe at Venue 405 after giving a sell-out, showstopping debut concert in the 2018 programme. There’s something for everyone as the band presents a varied programme of music and showcases its world-class soloists.
Venue: The Salvation Army Edinburgh City Corps
Venue description: Edinburgh City Corps is The Salvation Army at the heart of the City.  For the duration of the Fringe programme light refreshments will be available.  Afternoon teas will be served from 1pm-5pm on 19th-24th August.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access for wheelchair users available at the side-door entrance.  Accessible toilet

Title: Ayman Jarjour in Concert with John Coutts
Description: An evening of poetry and music given by John Coutts and Ayman Jarjour.  John is a published author and Poet-in-Residence at the Stirling Smith Art Gallery and Museum. Ayman is a Syrian classical guitarist who studied in Madrid and at Julliard, and has performed his music all over the world.  The concert is given in aid of the work of the local Salvation Army in Edinburgh, supporting its debt advice service and work supporting the recovery community.  An opportunity to chat with both artists will follow the performance.
Venue: The Salvation Army Edinburgh City Corps
Venue description: Edinburgh City Corps is The Salvation Army at the heart of the City.  For the duration of the Fringe programme light refreshments will be available.  Afternoon teas will be served from 1pm-5pm on 19th-24th August.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access for wheelchair users available at the side-door entrance.  Accessible toilet

Title: Joe Bor: The Story of Walter and Herbert
Description: Award-winning comedian Joe Bor retells the story of the friendship between his grandad (world-renowned town planner, Walter Bor) and his grandad's best friend (world-renowned comedy actor, Herbert Lom) and their journey from Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia to the UK. 'Natural born comic ability' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Joe Bor is a must see' (Alan Carr). 'Great at comedy' (Jack Whitehall).
Venue description: Come and graze in George Square! Food, drink, two fantastic venues and, of course, an upside-down purple cow. If you're looking for Udderbelly or Wee Coo, this is the place to be. We also have buzzing bars open 'til very late!
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Mandy Picks a Husband
Description: Almost 40 and totally single, Mandy takes us on a hilarious, raw 55-minute rollercoaster ride unearthing the magic elixir for her unmarried soul. Sell-out shows and rave reviews at the 2019 Hollywood Fringe Festival: winner of the Encore Producers’ Award and nominated for the Soaring Solo Artist Award. 'A tour-de-force performance and a must-see show...!' (Better-Lemons.com).
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival. Part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces, here we present three smart air-conditioned theatres, offering a selection of small to mid-scale theatre, musical theatre, comedy, sketch, improv, spoken word, a capella, music and cabaret. Stylish well stocked on-site bars give audiences the ultimate sense of occasion and comfort so rare on the fringe.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: A-Z Mental Health Atlas
Description: Can't tell a psychiatrist from a psychic or narcissistic personality disorder from an American President? An NHS shrink maps the psychiatric landscape in this WIP. Because our minds don't come with a satnav. 'Hilarious' (Buzzfeed.com)
Warnings:
Suicide and other taboo themes 
Other
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink - from breakfast through until late dinner. With a selection of free Fringe shows in three downstairs rooms throughout the day, it's a hive of Fringe activity in the middle of town with added bonus of all show spaces being fully air-conditioned and kids allowed until 10pm!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking. Steep hill to venue entrance

Title: 3,300 Miles – New Jersey to Edinburgh: A Transatlantic Songwriters' Circle
Description: UK meets USA in this song circle featuring acclaimed songwriters from New Jersey (Dan Sheehan, Andy Krikun) and Scotland (Seán McLaughlin, Annie Booth) exchanging stripped-down renditions of their songs and perspectives on songwriting in our current times.  The small hall at Lauriston Halls provides an intimate setting to hear our songwriters up close and personal.  Cumulatively, these four writers have been hailed in publications from the Los Angeles Times to The Scotsman and The Herald.  All ages welcome.
Artist: Songwriter/Musicians Annie Booth, Andy Krikun, Seán McLaughlin and Dan Sheehan.
Venue description: Lauriston Halls (both modernised) are situated between the Grassmarket and Tollcross, 10 minutes walk from Princes Street. The Large Hall has air conditioning and a sprung floor. It is a regular ceilidh (Scottish dance) venue popular with locals and visitors.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Bomb Happy D-Day 75
Description: A verbatim play about ordinary young men in extraordinary times. Bomb Happy evocatively brings to life the powerful testimonies of five Normandy Veterans, inexperienced young conscripts who find themselves part of one of the most dangerous operations of World War II. As the action unfolds, memories – humorous and harrowing – collide, allowing a close-up experience of life on the front line, whilst wives’ accounts highlight the lifelong impact of PTSD.  Post-show Meet the Veterans at Friday and Saturday performances.
Venue: Army @ The Fringe in Association with Summerhall
Venue description: The Army invites you into our home, a real-life Army Reserve Centre in Edinburgh’s New Town. Programmed and run in association with Summerhall, Edinburgh’s most daring and respected year-round multi-arts venue, Army@The Fringe is staffed by serving soldiers. The relaxed and comfortable Mess Bar serves hot and cold drinks and alcoholic beverages along with an Army Tuckshop throughout the day and evening.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking

Title: Josh Widdicombe: Work in Progress
Description: Ahead of his nationwide tour, Josh returns to Edinburgh for a strictly limited run of work-in-progress shows. It'll feature grumbles and jokes which tackle the hot comedy topics of advent calendars, pesto and the closing time of his local park. 'His talent for comedy is priceless' (Evening Standard).
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in 17 venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman). Open until 03:00.

The five Studios have some of the best audience facilities on the Fringe, with comfortable modern seating, and the indoor Studios Bar has plenty of sofas, a much used piano and serves freshly prepared hot and cold meals.  The Flick at Underground can also be found here.

Title: Eddie Izzard: Wunderbar (Preview)
Description: A preview of Wunderbar ahead of a UK and Ireland Tour.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces and six bars. A must for all Fringe-goers. A massive mini-Fringe under one roof, this iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe!
Venue accessibility: For further information about accessibility at Gilded Balloon venues email accessibility@gildedballoon.co.uk. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The building is accessed by eight steps or an external platform lift. For further information visit www.gildedballoon.co.uk/accessibility

Title: Angus Brown: Everest
Description: Every dead body on Mount Everest was once a very motivated person... At the freezing cold base of Everest, used-car salesman Albert Bentwater readies himself to attempt one of the most brutal physical feats of endurance known to humankind – the summit of Mount Everest. But things can get a little foggy in the death zone, and for Albert/Angus the ice could be getting a little thin... In a show that is part stand-up and part stage show, comedian Angus Brown attempts to do the impossible – summit Mount Everest, live, from a warm stage in Edinburgh.
Venue description: Imagination Workshop, George Street, is situated in the historic 4* George Hotel. Located within walking distance of Edinburgh Waverley train station, and a stone’s throw from the bus station and airport tram. Featuring three beautiful and atmospheric spaces that will set the scene to any show. In-house coffee shop, restaurant, and bar. All spaces are wheelchair accessible.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: ETBF – Stonemasonry Demonstration
Description: A practical demonstration from Stone Federation GB. Expert demonstration and guidance on stone repairs and replacement. Highlighting the need to ensure correct stone, and mortar, selection and why this is so important.
Venue description: Courtyard of the Edinburgh World Heritage Trust.

Title: Cerys Bradley and Rachel Wheeley: The Unfortunate Bisexual
Description: What does it mean to be bisexual? No, actually, what does it mean? Are we doing it right? How can you tell? Join us for an hour of comedy as confusing as coming out. As ridiculous as explaining the ins and outs of attraction to everyone you meet. There will be jokes, tangents and graphs, because why have one thing when you can have many? 'The perfect hosts' (Evening Standard).
Artist: The Unfortunate Bisexual / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A lively and trendy gay-friendly cafe/bar venue. Situated over two floors for eating, drinking and dancing. Now open until 3am. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our function room from 12noon-midnight. Over 18s only.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet. Level access to bar. There are 10 steps down to the performance space & toilets

Title: Jennifer Tyler: Ready or Not
Description: For years, Jennifer liked to be over-prepared. Every move was meticulously thought-through and every possible outcome was assessed. She was always really really ready. It took being offered a slot at the Fringe at the last minute for her to realise that she’d never be “ready” – no one ever is. So, she threw her rule book out the window and here she is! Through a joyous, warm-hearted mix of music and conversational comedy, Jennifer takes us on her unique journey of fear, bravery, cheese hangovers and what happened when she finally just said yes!
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in 17 venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman). Open until 03:00.

Title: Citizens of Nowhere?
Description: A funny, moving real-time live audio drama by award-winning writer, Ming Ho. British-Chinese matriarch Linda Lo shares news with her son, Jun Chi and daughter, Jane; but Jane has big news too, while Jun Chi is mystified by Linda’s refusal to discuss plans for his upcoming wedding. This intimate performance by actors seated among the audience is experienced through headphones, as if eavesdropping, and includes light refreshments.  The production premièred at Southbank Centre in October 2018 and had a sold-out run at Duddell’s London during CAN Festival 2019. Complimentary drink on arrival. Part of FeastFest.
Venue address: 80 Lauriston Place, Novotel Edinburgh Centre Hotel
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the Festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Grassmarket. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and fantastic food.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There is a small hill when approaching from the Grassmarket

Title: Alcohol-Free Craic
Description: What’s better than one stand-up comedian for free? That’s right, two stand-up comedians for free. Richard Wright (2011 Eastenders Christmas episode carol-singing extra) and Aideen McQueen (off the telly in Ireland) bring you an hour of funny that’s well worth your money. At the end. It’s free to get in. (PS – Only Richard and Aideen won’t be drinking. Audience can totally have a drink. And should!)
Artist: Aideen McQueen and Richard Wright / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: 1428, Cowgate gets its name from medieval times when cattle were herded down the street on market day. Now, fast forward to today; The Carnivore compliments the heritage of Edinburgh’s meat market and this is where our ethos of great quality meat for unbeatable value was born. The fuss-free food features authentic meat-lover’s classics with a twist, paired with American-inspired whiskey cocktail. Free Fringe comedy every day during August Fringe.

Title: The Sacrifice
Description: Prepare for the most epic spectacle you will ever experience. The sword shall be drawn. Blood shall be spilt. The ritual shall commence. They are waiting for you... Created and performed by Norwegian Gaulier-trained clown duo, Steffen Hånes and Sigmund Fosli Lillefjære, the show is a hilarious mess of clown and absurd comedy, directed by Izzy Stott. Audience reviews 2018: 'Wonderful, hugely entertaining'. 'A clever and subtle interpretation of clowning'.
Artist: Sigmund Fosli Lillefjære, Steffen Hånes, Kissing Cousins, PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: Opium alternative bar and nightclub is Edinburgh's longest running dedicated rock venue. Open seven days a week until 5am, Opium offers the very best in alternative entertainment. From rockaoke to live bands. During the Fringe we host a wide selection of top, five-star PBH Free Fringe comedy. Over 18s only.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. There are two steps into the bar area and downstairs room. There are then 10 steps to upstairs room

Title: Apocalypse Comedy Club featuring Mick Neven
Description: The award-winning Aussie comedian is back with a brand-new show, taking on the end of the world. If anyone can make the coming Apocalypse funny – Nevvo can. Now with added survival tips. 'Bags of dark humour, expertly executed' ***** (Issuu.com/BunburyMagazine, Edinburgh). ‘A rollercoaster Wizard of a ride from Oz’ (InternationalTimes.it, Edinburgh).
Venue description: Bannermans is one of Edinburgh's premier live music venues, located in the heart of the historic Old Town. A proven firm favorite with locals and tourists for many years now. Open from 12:00-01:00 every day, apart from Sundays when we open at 12:30. No under 18s. www.bannermanslive.co.uk

Title: Adam Flood and Blake AJ: Joke Boys
Description: A stand-up comedy show with two halves, by two comedians united by the powerful force of convenience. One has an afro, the other is a cheeky Northerner, and they are both boys with jokes. 'Good mood comedy, easy access escapism and inclusive funniness' (BN1Magazine.co.uk). Nominee for BBC New Comedian of the Year 2019.
Artist: Adam Flood and Blake AJ / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: A friendly neighbourhood bar with a great choice of craft, cask beers, wines and spirits, friendly staff and a delicious new menu. Last orders during Fringe: 3am. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our function room from 12noon-midnight.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible. Single step from street into bar. Level access once inside

Title: Terry Alderton: Bingo Bango
Description: 'The comedy thrill of a lifetime' ***** (Scotsman). 'A comedian of dizzying inventiveness' ***** (Times). Edinburgh’s favourite, award-winning, unpredictable comedian is here for outright laughs and you're invited along for the ride. A blistering new show that captures the true spirit of the Fringe. No politics, no message, just an hour of stand-up comedy and chaos from one of the best in the business.. And someone will win a car! As seen on Live At The Apollo, Michael McIntyre’s Roadshow, Dave’s One Night Stand and star of BBC Radio 4’s Terry Alderton Show.
Venue description: Monkey Barrel Comedy is on Blair Steet in Edinburgh's Old Town, bringing you the best acts in the best rooms at this year's Fringe.

Title: Homer to Hip Hop: A History of Spoken Word
Description: A fun and fascinating tour of the oral tradition and the poetic movements that have shaped history presented by a former National Poetry Slam Champion. From the oral tradition to the Edinburgh Fringe, from Virgil to Biggy Smalls, meet the poetic movements that have shaped history.  Why have wordsmiths always been vilified, feared and revered? This fun and fascinating performance lecture follows July’s release of the groundbreaking new book Stage Invasion: Poetry & the Spoken Word Renaissance.
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. Over 18s only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Elisa (Elisa Toffoli)
Description: Multi-platinum Italian singing sensation Elisa has been honing her skills as a songwriter and artist since the release of her debut album in 1997. Since then, she's sung with Pavarotti, performed twice at The Winter Olympics and won several Italian music awards. Catch her at The Liquid Rooms, Edinburgh on Friday 2nd August.

Title: After Vibe

Title: Underwater
Description: A show in the dark. Sea creatures and humans face the environmental apocalypse. In these three short plays, jellyfish fight turtles, killer whales discuss veganism, and prawns tickle people. Yet this is not so absurd, if compared to our everyday life. The characters challenge the viewer to look for sense – to look in the dark, to go underwater. *** (NorthWestEnd.co.uk). Award-winning theatre company, 2017 Greater Manchester Fringe.

Title: Never Heard of It
Description: Never-before-seen nonsense on stage. Seven Gaulier-trained performers from around the world will try their best to keep you alive, entertained and hopefully laughing. In this cabaret-style clown show, less-than-intellectual characters create a new and ridiculous mess, every night, just for you. You won’t learn anything, you won’t regret anything. You will have fun.
Warnings: Audience Participation, Scenes of a Sexual Nature, Strong Language/Swearing
Artist: Never Heard of Them / Laughing Horse Free Festival

Title: Being Liza
Description: A new play with music by Rachel Flynn. Being Liza is an original story about a girl in a pivotal transition of her life, discovering who she really is behind the mask of an icon. Frances Edwards is Scotland's premiere Liza Minnelli tribute act. Her dad Pete is her demanding manager and co-star, blindly focused on their ultimate success. Fusing classic Liza Minnelli songs such as New York, New York and Cabaret. 'An experience you won't forget... a stunning and beautifully judged comedy drama... a smart and sensitive study of a young woman on the cusp' ***** (ScotsGay.co.uk).
Venue description: Just Festival events aim to challenge perceptions, celebrate differences and promote respectful dialogue. The conversations, talks, exhibitions and performances which constitute Just’s annual programme are designed to engage with topical local, national and international questions of social justice, equality and identity, including prejudice against race, ethnicity, class and economic status. Just explores these issues by creating safe spaces for dialogue and exchange between affected groups.

Description: Tim Key from Peep Show, Partridge, Taskmaster and his own BAFTA-nominated Wonderdate, brings new poems to Edinburgh. ‘He is a genius plan and simple’ ***** (Time Out). ‘This is sublime, busy and evocative work from a man who keeps getting better and better’ ***** (List). Edinburgh Comedy Award winner a few years ago.

Title: Cowboys, Country Music and Queers
Description: Stand-up comedy and storytellin’ with Brandon Burke. A not to miss limited run of Brandon’s funny and fearless journey from the Ozarks to London. An honest and joyous romp of rednecks, bigots and big haired country women. Come laugh along as this award-winning comedian spins a yarn of choosing among belt-buckles, bibles, Broadway musicals and Bo Duke. Brandon's story is unique to the Fringe, full of country humour and well crafted honest stories.
Venue description: Imagination Workshop, George Street, is situated in the historic 4* George Hotel. Located within walking distance of Edinburgh Waverley train station, and a stone’s throw from the bus station and airport tram. Featuring three beautiful and atmospheric spaces that will set the scene to any show. In-house coffee shop, restaurant, and bar. All spaces are wheelchair accessible.

Title: Generation Whyyy?
Description: My feet hurt. I’m cold. I’ve no internet. I’m hungry. My phone’s dying. My vape’s dead. I can’t deal. Pose. Flash. Filter. Post. Wait. Anticipate. React. Delete. Cry in a pillow. Repeat. We are the new Boomers, Millennials, Snowflakes. We are Generation Y. We are Generation Whyyy do I have to wait? Whyyy do I have to get up before 12pm? Whyyy do I only have 999 likes? Whyyy is life so hard? Whyyy?!
Venue description: Imagination Workshop, George Street, is situated in the historic 4* George Hotel. Located within walking distance of Edinburgh Waverley train station, and a stone’s throw from the bus station and airport tram. Title: Encyclopedia of Kitchen Comedy Essays by Larry Tadlock
Description: Essays about growing up a Texan cattle-raising milk-drinking gay baptist, to become a barefoot plant-based health coach. From zen monk, to theatre in Boulder, to grass-eating stand-up in Hollywood. Binging on doughnuts to millet cleanses, testing every health food system and becoming one with nature, while still trying to remain worldly.  The search to be present continues to be a disaster.  Hilarious memooir about one man's move to vegan.  Includes Q&A. Often compared to David Sedaris.  Has Performed with Gotham Comedy, Improv Comedy Store and the Groundlings.
Venue: PBH's Free Fringe @ Natural Food Kafe

Title: Sowhereto Africa: Free to Dance
Description: Old and new beats meet performance poetry paying tribute to South Africa’s legends. Experience the sounds and rhythms of the Soweto street life, with its contagious energy and invigorating vibes, through an everyman’s daily journey. The production utilises live music, dance, street footage and performance poetry to tell stories and engage audiences with traditional and modern South African cultures. Njobo Productions and African Connections CIC are returning to the Edinburgh Fringe due to popular demand. 'The cast performs continuously, fully invested in sharing their love of dance and their culture from South Africa’ (FringeReview.co.uk).
Artist: Njobo Productions and African Connections CIC
Venue description: A beautifully restored Grade B listed building, showcasing many of the unique features of what was originally the St Thomas’s Episcopal Church. The Ghillie Dhu enjoys an enviable location, tucked in the west end of Edinburgh city centre. The venue hosts live music in the main bar offering a truly Scottish experience in the heart of the city.

Title: Journeys of the Mind and the Megabus
Description: Joe Bates (BBC Radio 4 Extra, 6 Music) and Luke Chilton (BBC Radio 4, Radio 4 Extra) have both been on a journey: one into the recesses of a broken mind in a foreign land, the other on a coach on the M1 southbound. Their journeys made them what they are – find out what that is in this brilliant split-bill stand-up show!

Title: Passion and Rhythm
Description:
From passionate melodies to captivating modern beats, this piano concert performed by the eclectic Italian artist Sonja Toja will at first take you through some of the most significant authors of romanticism, such as Chopin, Schumann and Brahms, whereas the second part will be dedicated to international folk music, with the exotic sharp rhythms of Bartòk’s Bulgarian dances to finish with Ginastera’s Argentinian dances.
After graduating from the Conservatory of Music of Milan, Sonja performed extensively in Italy, Germany, US, UK and Luxemburg, while attending masterclasses with Italian and international masters such as Ballista, Balzani, Petruschanski and Deutsch.
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances – from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music – and some book discussions. Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the delightful Georgian interior.

Description: Achtung! Achtung! Comedian Al Murray and historian James Holland are bringing their highly acclaimed World War II podcast to the Edinburgh Festival. We Have Ways of Making You Talk has established a firm beach head in the British podcast charts as the two men tell battlefield tales and bring forgotten events back into sharp focus. Al and James will present the podcast live as they decide who was the baddest Nazi of them all and describe some of the more extraordinary stories of the war.
Venue description: This classic building in the heart of the New Town is now the centre of a fantastic Festival hub which is host to some of the finest theatre, comedy and music from around the world. Description: Deepu Dileepan presents a string of wildly hilarious stories that deconstructs belongingness in present day society. Featuring recitations from the holy book and combo meals at McDonalds, enter the world of the outsider. Deeply personal and flippantly political at once. Raiser Theatre's vibrant young cast bring you Linda McLean's blackly comic short play of a grown-up brother and sister who exact revenge on their violent father. Locking him in the coal shed as retribution for years of sniping, bullying and pain, they are both aching to use their fists on him for once. But he's not defeated – yet.

Title: Depthless Observations
Description: Ollie and Josh are two lovely guys, who it’d be a pleasure to spend an afternoon with. Ollie is just an average man desperately trying to find something unique about himself. And Josh is really tall and just wants to be happy. Both graduates of the Soho Theatre Young Company, both failed actors, but that doesn’t stop them from ploughing on in the world of stand-up. Join them, and and potentially some special guests, for an afternoon of larks.

Title: BBC and HighTide Radio Plays
Description: HighTide, BBC Radio 3 and BBC Arts present two interweaving plays, written by talented writers Vinay Patel (Doctor Who) and Tallulah Brown (Songlines). These new works, written as radio plays, have been created in tandem and have a playful rapport. Vinay Patel’s The Shores tells the story of enduring humanity over 8,000 years, and complements Brown's Silver Darlings that centres on a mystical mermaid, examining how first sinking into the depths of the unknown is the way back to the surface.

When children start giddily pounding on drums, the happy banging and exciting beats show Chinese-Korean children’s positive attitude and joyful lives. Mulan – Mulan is one of many great Chinese heroes. Simple yet brave, she joined the army to replace her father and protect her home and country. Her actions prove that girls can be just as good as boys.

To find his own Corner of the Sky, he goes on a tumultuous journey of self-discovery, exploring all that life has to offer. Title: Qoya Women's Movement Workshops
Description: Qoya is a women's movement practice that combines yoga, free dance and sensual movement to bring women back into their bodies, to remember our essence is wise, wild and free. In Qoya, we focus on how it feels, not how it looks. There is no way to do it "right", the only way you know, is that it feels good. You don't need any movement or dance experience to participate. Wear loose comfortable clothing. Workshops will be facilitated by Australian dancer and certified Qoya teacher, Erin Fowler. Find more information at www.qoya.love.

Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance and visual arts for people of all ages in the atmospheric buildings of Edinburgh’s former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College. There’s delicious food and drink in our own Royal Dick bar and Summerhall Café, plus al fresco bars and street food in the buzzing festival courtyard. The full programme of performance and exhibitions is at www.summerhall.co.uk
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces and the Basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

Description: Enjoy some authentic flamenco passion in our ever-popular show. Bursting with raw emotion and explosive rhythms, this is a fiesta of pure dance, music and intensity that brings the best of a real Andalucian night. Just like a traditional Spanish penya, you don't watch but experience the fiery guitar and percussive dancing, and get carried away on wave after wave of tragic and joyous vocals. Featuring some top talents brought in directly from Spain, this show brings a modern twist to the classic flamenco tradition. 'Powerful dance, frenetic guitar, pulsating rhythms' ***** (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Flamenco and world music/dance venue alongside a tasty Spanish tapas cafe/bar. The venue is located in the busy Southside area of Edinburgh, offering a programme of music, dance and story telling for adults and children. Great music, great Spanish food and a great atmosphere!
Venue accessibility: small venue. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, Reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking. bar/cafe. Entrance to the venue at red corner door

Title: Sense of Tumour
Description: What does a busy, modern, single woman do when she finds a lump in her breast? She cracks jokes. With no respect for cancer, Ingibjorg has spent most of her cancer treatment writing jokes to stay in control of an otherwise daunting situation, making people giggle nervously about her blue tit, baldness and bowel movements and revealing way too much about getting laid with cancer. Now fresh out of chemo, she's raring to overshare stuff with a brave enough audience. With special guests.
Warnings: Contains Distressing Themes, Scenes of a Sexual Nature, Strong Language/Swearing
Venue description: An easy-going hangout with simple food and a back room with floor mattresses and afternoon movies. Plus a selection of board games, dartboard and arcade machine, there’s plenty to do besides drink at the Brass Monkey. However, the drinks alone, which are cheaper than usual and come with a student discount, keep the bar busy and the Free Fringe shows fill the cinema room each afternoon.

Title: Love and Sex and All Things In-Between
Description: Verbatim stories of "love" in all its magnificence and monstrousness.
Warnings: Contains Distressing Themes, Scenes of a Sexual Nature, Strong Language/Swearing
Venue description: Hugely popular Royal Mile venue located at the very heart of the festival. Part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces. With a reputation for award-winning shows, the three smart air-conditioned theatres offer the very best shows & entertainment at the Festival. Ultra stylish on-site bars provide the perfect way to start, or end, your night. Style and Class on the fringe. For more info/show info see: www.thespaceuk.com

Title: Daniel Audritt: Better Man
Description: Award-winning comedian, writer and co-creator of Comedy Central's Modern Horror Stories, Daniel Audritt brings his much-anticipated debut hour to the Fringe. Having previously written for 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown, Mock the Week, Comic Relief, The News Quiz, Dead Ringers, NewsJack and many more, the show will be punchline-heavy stand-up comedy show that questions love, relationships, modern masculinity and what it takes to be a good guy. Dave's fourth Best Joke of the Fringe 2018. 'A winning wit' (Bruce Dessau, BeyondTheJoke.co.uk).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue description: Best Small Venue in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the Fringe!

Title: Avalanche
Description: No matter how long the winter – spring is sure to follow. A story about journeys, routine, missed moments, pain, irrational thoughts, assumptions, fear, surprising compassion, screens, memories, loneliness, coffee and unlikely friendships. It’s about how we connect with those around us even on the smallest level and the impact we have on others without knowing it. It’s about seasons and change and how nothing ever stays the same. But mostly it’s about hope and how finding those moments of connection make the world a better place.
Venue description: An unrivalled location at the heart of the festival. Part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces, here we present three smart air-conditioned theatres, offering a selection of small to mid-scale theatre, musical theatre, comedy, sketch, improv, spoken word, a capella, music and cabaret. Stylish well stocked on-site bars give audiences the ultimate sense of occasion and comfort so rare on the fringe.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Ahab; or What If Moby Dick Were Stand-Up Comedy
Description: Moby Dick: a book, a play, an episode of Star Trek, 12 movies and a fish. Now, it's been adapted into a stand-up comedy show by niche idiot Jonny Gillam. He wondered: 'If we can adapt books into plays, can we adapt them into stand-up? I don't know. Still, if anyone's going to fail at this, I'd like it to be me.' The result is a show that is entirely Moby Dick and entirely stand-up. Expect hubristic rants, musings on the minutiae of technical objects and Dick jokes.
Venue description: We welcome you to The Raging Bull, an Edinburgh Cocktail Bar famous for its Coffee Cocktails. Our cosy bar is inspired by the eccentric yet good natured fellow, who has become accustomed to drinking his cocktails in comfortable and stylish surroundings. So expect rustic walls, marble tables, natural foliage and walls adorned with pictures of the handsome Bull when you visit us, plus free Fringe shows downstairs daily.

Title: Lew Fitz: Chucky Egg (Work in Progress)
Description: With his first solo show, stand-up comedian Lew Fitz (BBC New Comedy Award nominee 2018) covers a hilarious and often uncommon journey from his northern, working-class background all the way to the Deep South of America and back again. Expect stories of masculinity, regret, shame and downright silliness in forty-five minutes, from a highly tipped 'engaging... nimble and vibrant (Chortle.co.uk) performer who has to face his past to forge his future.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Mash House
Venue description: Fringe Venue number 288
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking. Hidden just off Cowgate on the stairway joining Cowgate and Guthrie Street

Title: The Sinners Club
Description: Where can you go to find all the dirty scandals on campus? The Sinners Club is the only radio show where people can call in anonymously and tell the whole university their biggest sins from a dirty night out. Accidentally On Purpose (sponsored by the Goldsmiths Drama Society) presents The Sinners Club, a fast-paced comedy that explores what it means to make mistakes, deal with regrets and suffer from terrible hangovers after being so hammered you couldn’t remember your own name. Hangovers. Mistakes. Utter tunes. What more do you need?
Venue description: Next door to theSpace @ Surgeons Hall, theSpaceTriplex makes up part of our fabulously smart destination hub of 10 performance spaces located right at the heart of the modern Fringe and offers an unmissable platform of diverse live performance. Music, dance, theatre, physical theatre, a capella, opera, comedy and cabaret. A vibrant programme of performance, all under one roof in the most spectacular space in town.

Title: Standard:Elite
Description: There are two types of ticket. Everyone gets a Standard ticket. You have to earn an Elite ticket. Together, we're going to tell a story... of a girl from Lowground spun from spiderweb and a boy from Highground carved from clouds. Standards work to build the story, Elites control which path the story takes. That's fair, right? Standard:Elite is a playful, interactive theatre experience about class and privilege that's irreverent, accessible and fun. There are two types of ticket. There aren't two types of people. ***** (VoiceMag.uk). ***** (TheSpyInTheStalls.co.uk). Winner: Best New Writing (Manchester Fringe), Best Newcomer (Brighton Fringe).
Venue description: A unique theatre in a converted church in the heart of Edinburgh, Bedlam Theatre returns to the Fringe for its 39th year with another exciting and eclectic programme of theatre and comedy. Bedlam Theatre offers several captioned performances.  The dates of these performances will be released in due course.

Our performance times, and those times the accessible entrance will be opened, will be detailed both on our website and on a sign outside of the entrance to the auditorium. Assistance from staff will be available

Title: Matt Stellingwerf: Sisyphus
Description: As punishment for his self-aggrandising craftiness and deceitfulness, Sisyphus was forced to roll an immense boulder up a hill only for it to roll down whenever it neared the top, consigning him to an eternity of useless efforts and unending frustration. Join award-winning comedian Matt Stellingwerf as he rolls his own boulder... searching for meaning in a life, seemingly, wasted. From his worthless PhD to his obsession with Wikipedia. From the pointless lies he tells to the hubris of thinking he's worth listening to in the first place. Is there joy to be found in uselessness? Maybe...
Venue description: A fashionable newly refurbished cafe-bar right in the centre of town, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, open daily for food and drink - from breakfast through until late dinner. With a selection of free Fringe shows in three downstairs rooms throughout the day, it's a hive of Fringe activity in the middle of town with added bonus of all show spaces being fully air-conditioned and kids allowed until 10pm!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking. Steep hill to venue entrance

Title: Window
Description: How do you confess your wildest dreams when words fall short? Follow the journey of Xingxing, the boy from the stars, as he's thrust into the midst of city life.  With opportunities alive, Xingxing struggles to find his place of belonging and school life is no exception. Bullied for eccentricities, an unlikely encounter uncovers hidden talents and the chance to finally discover himself. Will Xingxing find his voice and a way for us to sing together? Let seven Chinese children hold you in their warm embraces, as the whole world dreams together. Where words fail, music surely speaks.
Venue description: Paradise Green is at the heart and soul of the largest arts festival in the world, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, relax with a drink from our snack bar before your performance and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The building is accessed from George IV Bridge, which has a wide pavement

Title: Hard Truths – An Improvised Play
Description: Never seen before... never to be seen again! UoN Improv Society presents Hard Truths, a completely improvised one-act play. The show is about finding the funny out of our real lives; our performers giving completely honest confessions provoked by an audience suggestion of a question to inform the rest of the play. No scripts, no pre-planning, just eight performers and a stage. Anything can happen, so what are you waiting for?
Venue description: Greenside @ Nicolson Square is set in the heart of town, seconds from the Festival Theatre, the flashing lights of Bristo Square and the hustle and bustle of the Royal Mile. We’re bringing our desire for creating great spaces and passion for service to the heart of the festival.
Venue accessibility: Venue underwent a full multi-million pound refurbishment in 2013 making the whole site accessible. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Old Town Historical Walking Tour
Description: This tour will take you into parts of Edinburgh that you did not know existed, off the tourist trail. From hidden Victorian gardens to centuries-old buildings with plenty of story attached. Hear about how the first skyscrapers in the world were built in Edinburgh. Indeed, we hosted the tallest buildings in the world long before any other country caught on to the trend. Find out who the famous local criminal was that became the inspiration for Jekyll and Hyde. Learn where the word Black Market came from and where Ebeneezer Scrooge is buried (yes, really).
Venue description: An old police box, opposite Starbucks and next to the Tron Kirk. All of our tours/shows start here.
