Description: Explore Edinburgh Sherlock style! A succession of clues and puzzles will lead you to find the truth about Sherlock Holmes and his connection to the city of Edinburgh. The game takes an average of 2.5 hours. Less or more depending on the agility of the deduction work. It covers a good portion of the historic New Town and some other wonderful places off the tourist trail. All you need is one ticket per group (seven people max). A refundable deposit of £20 is requested for the renting of the kit.
Warnings:
Requires a phone with internet access. Child friendly but hard for children, especially under 12. People arriving late may not be admitted. The game finishes far from where it starts. The game will finish in the West End of the city.
Involves Walking, Other
Venue description: Meeting point.

Title: Fright Bus Service
Description: A theatrical sightseeing tour on-board a classic 1960s Routemaster bus, taking you on a journey around the darker side of Europe’s most haunted city. Join your creepy conductor and a peculiar psychic investigator on a hilarious trip around the ancient city’s sites of murder, torture, execution and paranormal activity. From the makers of the Edinburgh Ghost Bus Tours comes this comedy horror show you’ll never forget as you travel around the city and discover its dark and unusual secrets. 'Far better than much of the Fringe' (Edinburgh-Reviews.co.uk).
Venue description: A black classic 1960s Routemaster bus transformed into a theatre space, with cameras, screens, audio/visual capabilities and seating for up to 64 audience members. Beautiful interior.
Venue accessibility: Due to the classic design of the bus itself it is not wheelchair accessible unless the wheelchair can be folded and kept close to the audience member as they're sitting on the bus. Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking. Upper deck. The black bus is situated on Waverley Bridge

Title: A Famous Taste of Scotland Dinner and Show
Description: A fun-packed feast of traditional music, dance, song and myth with historic Prestonfield House and the magnificent setting for this nightly dinner show. From the bagpiper's traditional welcome in the grounds through fiddles, drums and ceilidh dancing to a grand finale with the Three Scottish Tenors this is a packed evening of traditional Scottish entertainment. Sword dances, fiddles, song and legend will entertain all ages. Enjoy great photo opportunities, a gourmet four-course dinner with wine and a taste of haggis in a splendid setting just a few minutes from the Royal Mile.
Venue description: The circular Georgian Stables of historic Prestonfield House are set in gardens and parlkland adjacent to Royal Holyrood Park and Arthur's Seat.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: West End Producer – Free Willy
Description: Join West End Producer as he auditions special guests for his Free Willy musical. You, the audience, are on the panel as WEP challenges guests to perform such iconic whale-based hits including: My Willy Needs to Be Wet and One Whale More. Interspersed with theatrical musings, WEP will teach you the perfect jazz hand technique, how to bow properly, and gives one lucky person the chance to win some genuine, worn West End show pants. 'Bring on the movie, dear' ***** (Jonathan Baz). 'Prepare to be shocked, rocked and mocked' (Michael Ball).
Warnings: Audience Participation, Involves Walking, Strong Language/Swearing
Artist: Cuffe and Taylor in association with Jason Haigh-Ellery
Venue description: Assembly Checkpoint is the Fringe's premier venue for cabaret, music and more. The venue is located inside an old church and exudes warmth and charm. There is a bar inside the upstairs venue and further drinking and dining options downstairs.
Venue accessibility: Large flight of 26 stone steps up to the performance venue, which is on the first floor. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Time Please
Description: 'The writing is fabulously blackly comic and timed to perfection' (Deirdre O'Halloran, Literary Associate Soho Theatre). 'Keith: Every one of us colours things with the crayons that we have? Steve: God Keith, you don't half talk b******s sometimes'. Keith Goodman is a wronged man. He’s lost his kids, his house, his Playstation... oh and his wife, and none of it is his fault. Shambolic and drunk, Keith hatches a plan to share his plight with the world and so begins a night that sees ever-appeasing barman, Steve and his feisty wife, Cath in a lock-in like no other.
Venue description: Winner of Best Venue for 2018 (Theatre Weekly’s Best of The Fest), PQA Venues is set in the stunning grade A listed Riddles Court situated on the Royal Mile. Offering three diverse performance spaces showcasing the best in theatre and comedy. With our bar and food courtyard set amongst a brand new yurt structure, PQA Venues is the go-to destination for 2019.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access into the ground floor venues. First floor venues are accessed via a lift and with Q 2 being level access and Q! access via 4 steps which can be ramped for additional access needs

Title: Martin Bearne and Joe McTernan: Milk and Two
Description: Join two of Scotland's fastest rising comics for a fun hour of stand-up comedy. Martin Bearne is a two-time Scottish Comedian of the Year finalist and master of dark comedy. 'Killer one-liners' (Scotsman). 'Master of delivery' (SomethingFunnyEdinburgh.wordpress.com). 'Genuinely killer lines' (Daniel Sloss). Joe McTernan has supported Tom Stade on tour, co-created the online sitcom M.U.F.F alongside Daniel Sloss and Tom Stade, and has also featured on BBC Short Stuff. 'His punchlines hit home...sure to delight with his amusing frustration' (EdFestMag.com).
Venue description: A secret hidden gem over two floors. Nightcap is a cosy cocktail restaurant.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking

Title: The Long Look
Description:
A collaboration between painter Audrey Grant and photographer/printmaker Norman McBeath which explores the art of portraiture beyond the conventional artist and sitter relationship through their unique creative exchange. Audrey asked Norman to sit for a charcoal portrait, and at the end of each sitting, Norman photographed the sketch and the creative environment, including her hands, his chair and the charcoal. She would then erase the drawing, leaving charcoal traces behind, and begin the portrait anew. The finished portraits, which took two years to complete, as well as another portrait of Norman and two portraits of award-winning crime writer Val McDermid, will be on display in this fascinating and revelatory exhibition.
 Part of the Edinburgh Art Festival. Exhibition runs 25 May – 27 October 2019 | Mon – Sun: 10am – 5pm

Title: The Welcome Hearth – Passing It On!
Description: An opening night of Scots and Traveller tradition in song and story welcomes our guests. With First Nations protocol and Scottish hospitality. Donald Smith hosts storytellers Jess Smith, James Spence, Janis Mackay and Heather Yule.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Mile to the Museum & National Museum of Scotland
Description:
Discover the story of Scotland through our capital city and National Museum. Explore key locations and stories hidden around the Royal Mile. See a city of the past – which goes unnoticed for many – where commoners, queens and criminals once walked. Then tour the National Museum of Scotland to view our nation’s treasures, stepping through Scotland’s history, exploring how special objects have shaped our past, present and future.
 Suitable for all ages 5+ Tickets: www.mercattours.com | £25, including tea & scone at the Museum.
 Departs from Mercat Cross, beside St. Giles' Cathedral.
 Tour involves cobbled streets, slopes and stairs. The guide will always adapt the route to visitor’s needs. Full access statement here.

Title: In Conversation with Joseph Naytowhow
Description: Discover the fascinating backgrounds of our guests with insights from Scottish based hosts. Hailing from Saskatchewan, Cree First Nation storyteller Joseph Naytowhow is welcomed by storyteller David Campbell.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Open Hearth
Description: Storytellers and musicians gather round the hearth for a relaxed traditional session of stories from home and abroad, as the darkness closes in and minds glow with pictures in the symbolic fire. The perfect way to end your day! Hosted by Beverley Bryant, with guest storytellers Joseph Naytowhow from Canada, Alexandria Patience and Donald McNeill.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Enchanted Garden
Description: Join Scottish and international storytellers and treat yourself with a relaxed afternoon of stories for all ages. Enjoy sessions in the Botanic Cottage, find the cosy spots where stories are shared and enjoy story journeys around the beautiful surroundings, immersed in autumn colours.
Venue address: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, Arboretum Place, Edinburgh

Title: In Conversation with Heidi Dahlsveen
Description: Discover the fascinating backgrounds of our guests with insights from Scottish-based hosts. Norwegian storyteller Heidi Dahlsveen is welcomed by Danish storyteller Svend-Erik Engh.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Scotland & Canada: Isobel Gunn
Description: In 1805, a young Orkney lass brazenly disguised herself as a boy and was hired as a labourer by the Hudson Bay Company. Their destination – the vast area of wilderness known as Rupert’s Land! This gruelling adventure is brought to life by Canadian storyteller Deborah Dunleavy, taking on the role of Isobel Gunn between 1805 – 1808 and the final days of her life some sixty years later. Based on true accounts, the piece unfolds as an epic storytelling poem set to orchestrated music by composer Howard Alexander. Developed with the support of Canada Council for the Arts.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Open Hearth
Description: Storytellers and musicians gather round the hearth for a relaxed traditional session of stories from home and abroad, as the darkness closes in and minds glow with pictures in the symbolic fire. The perfect way to end your day! Hosted by David Campbell, with guest storytellers Deborah Dunleavy from Canada, Heidi Dahlsveen from Norway and Svend-Erik Engh from Denmark.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Corryvreckan: Inspiralled Tales
Description: After a chance encounter with George Orwell’s son in the whirlpool that nearly killed him, storyteller Fiona Herbert was inspired to put her own spin on the maelstrom. Join her for myths reimagined, with Corryvreckan at their swirling heart. With live music and song from Sarah McFadyen.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Home, Heart & A Hint of Horror
Description: Savour the aromas of a Caribbean kitchen and swing from the branches of a Highland birchwood. Laugh, cry and occasionally curse with our most cherished yet challenging tales on a quest for belonging. Storytellers Jan Blake and Dougie Mackay explore the dearest, and sometimes darkest elements of family, heritage, heart and home.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Why Hamish Matters: Local Song in the Global Age
Description:
Ethnologist, singer and community activist Steve Byrne reflects on the essential work of Hamish Henderson’s collected local songs in areas of Scotland and how, through digitisation, they are being used for community development, considering ideas of cultural confidence, language, personal identity and localism in a globalised world.
 Tickets for National Library of Scotland events are available on eventbrite or 0131 623 3734. Book Your Ticket
Venue address: National Library of Scotland, George IV Bridge, Edinburgh

Title: In Conversation with Robert Seven Crows Bourdon
Description: Discover the fascinating backgrounds of our guests with insights from Scottish-based hosts. Coming from Quebec, Metis Mi’kmaq and Acadian storyteller Robert Seven Crows Bourdon is welcomed by Canadian storyteller Alette Willis.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: The Alan Bruford Lecture – Fenian Heroes at Sea
Description:
Already in some of the earliest surviving traces of the Fenian heroic tradition in medieval Irish literature, in similarly early references to historical Fianna, and in later Gaelic romance and folktale, there is the notion of travel across the sea. While heroes often undertake adventures abroad in other heroic story cycles, in this presentation we will consider the special significance of Fionn and his men in the maritime context.
 With Prof. Joseph Nagy.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Open Hearth
Description: Storytellers and musicians gather round the hearth for a relaxed traditional session of stories from home and abroad, as the darkness closes in and minds glow with pictures in the symbolic fire. The perfect way to end your day! Hosted by Canadian Dawne McFarlane, with guest storytellers Robert Seven Crows Bourdon and Louise Profeit-LeBlanc from Canada and Jackie Ross.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Garden of Tales: Stories from Lithuania
Description:
Step into the garden, luscious in summer and white with snow in winter. Sit under the blooming branches and taste the apple from the tree of life. Listen to stories from the worlds above, below and our own in between. Lithuanian storyteller Daiva Ivanauskaitė introduces us to traditional stories weaved with songs of her Baltic country as part of Lithuanian Days in Scotland. In partnership with Lithuanian Culture Institute and Lithuanian Embassy in the UK.
 For more information visit Lithuanian Art and Culture in the UK.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: In Conversation with Louise Profeit-LeBlanc
Description: Discover the fascinating backgrounds of our guests with insights from Scottish- based hosts. Hailing from the Yukon, Nacho Nyak Dun First Nation storyteller Louise Profeit-LeBlanc is welcomed by storyteller Jackie Ross.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Scotland & Canada: Stories from the Yukon
Description: Nacho Nyak Dun First Nation storyteller Louise Profeit-LeBlanc was nurtured by the traditional stories of her grandmother and has dedicated her life to collecting tales from elders in northern Yukon. Let her take you to the outskirts of the Arctic Circle as she shares these treasures.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Open Hearth
Description: Storytellers and musicians gather round the hearth for a relaxed traditional session of stories from home and abroad, as the darkness closes in and minds glow with pictures in the symbolic fire. The perfect way to end your day! Hosted by George Macpherson with music from Fin Moore, with guest storytellers Anamaria Lines from Brazil and Joseph Naytowhow from Canada.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: In Conversation with Michael Williams
Description: Discover the fascinating backgrounds of our guests with insights from Scottish- based hosts. Ontario storyteller Michael Williams is welcomed by storyteller Michael Kerins.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Scotland & Canada: Stories from the Great Plains
Description: Coming from the immense grasslands of Saskatchewan, Cree néhiyaw First Nation storyteller Joseph Naytowhow will transport you to the landscapes of the Great Plains, guiding you through their timeless sounds and stories.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Open Hearth
Description: Storytellers and musicians gather round the hearth for a relaxed traditional session of stories from home and abroad, as the darkness closes in and minds glow with pictures in the symbolic fire. The perfect way to end your day! Hosted by Michael Kerins, with guest storytellers Chuck Warren, Jess Smith and Daniel Serridge.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: A Close Shave! – Barber Shop Stories
Description:
Scottish barber and social satirist John Kay published his first caustic caricature in 1784. His biting wit and satirical style became so popular that Kay refurbished his barber’s shop to sell prints of his colourful clientele. There’s certainly a story behind every print, and many a close shave… Storytellers Jan Bee Brown and Beverley Casebow toast the entrepreneurs of the Enlightenment, from notorious publican John Dowie to dedicated follower of fashion Miss Sibilla Hutton, with audacious aeronauts, dodgy doctors and stony-broke bankers.
 Tickets for National Library of Scotland events are available on eventbrite or 0131 623 3734. Book Your Ticket
Venue address: National Library of Scotland, George IV Bridge, Edinburgh

Title: In Conversation with Margaret Grenier
Description: Discover the fascinating backgrounds of our guests with insights from Scottish-based hosts. Coming from British Columbia, Gitksan and Cree First Nation dancer and storyteller Margaret Grenier is welcomed by storyteller Marion Kenny.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Scotland & Canada: Stories from Newfoundland & Labrador
Description: Born and bred in Newfoundland and Labrador, Gary Green was raised on stories of life in the province prior to it becoming part of Canada. Join him for an evening rich with North Atlantic lore, where the boundary between folktales and early settlers’ life stories may blur.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Festival Guid Crack: Tales for Samhuinn
Description:
Samhuinn marks the time of year when the veil lifts between the worlds of darkness and light. Host storyteller Michael Williams invites you to celebrate Samhuinn with a feast of spooky tales featuring spirits, sprites and otherworldly characters. Fancy dress welcomed.
 Edinburgh’s long-running storytelling club meets on the last Friday of the month, upstairs in the Waverley Bar, St. Mary’s St.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High St, Edinburgh

Title: Open Hearth
Description: Storytellers and musicians gather round the hearth for a relaxed traditional session of stories from home and abroad, as the darkness closes in and minds glow with pictures in the symbolic fire. The perfect way to end your day! Hosted by Jess Smith with music from Calum Macleod, with guest storytellers Giovanna Conforto from Italy, George Macpherson and Bea Ferguson.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Family Samhuinn
Description: Make Samhuinn memorable for all the family and get into the Hallowe’en spirit with a bone chilling afternoon of stories, drama, games and songs to ensure youngsters can embrace the ancient traditions of the Beltane Fire Society.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Miss Lindsay’s Secret – The Yukon Letters
Description: Come in. Shut the Door. Open the Box. Concealed for over a century, the intimate tale of seamstress Minnie Lindsay will be revealed. Storyteller Maria MacDonell, reader Alan Finlayson and musician Georgina MacDonell Finlayson unwind threads of gold binding the gentle Glenesk hills to the heady Klondike.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Open Hearth
Description: Storytellers and musicians gather round the hearth for a relaxed traditional session of stories from home and abroad, as the darkness closes in and minds glow with pictures in the symbolic fire. The perfect way to end your day! Hosted by Margaret Bennett, with guest storytellers Gary Green and Margaret Grenier from Canada and James MacDonald Reid.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Canada Inspires
Description: Connect with nature the Canadian way. Folklorist Rosalind Kerven will explore how the time-honoured stories of Canada’s First Nations can motivate the environmental movement, inspired by her latest collection, ‘Native American Myths’. Deborah Dunleavy reflects on the stories of early settlers, while Linda Williamson weaves northern sky lore, the stars of autumn’s great Winged Horse and the Inuit creation of Sun and Moon.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Guisers Galore
Description:
Come along and join our storytellers to learn a song, a poem and a dance for real Hallowe’en guising, then follow the Old Town Guisers parade or prepare for guising in your local area.
 Rehearsals at the Scottish Storytelling Centre from 2pm with a performance at the Museum of Edinburgh at 3.30pm. Bring your own costume or mask. Not suitable for children under 5.
Venue: Scottish Storytelling Centre & Museum of Edinburgh
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High St, Edinburgh

Title: Scotland & Canada: Spirit & Tradition
Description: The Dancers of Damelahamid are an Indigenous dance company from British Columbia. Their rich history of masked dance inspires a compelling performance, celebrating the time, depth and diversity of Indigenous cultures across Canada. Through dramatic dance, captivating narrative, intricately carved masks and elaborate regalia, the Dancers of Damelahamid transform time and space, bridging the ancient with living tradition.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Beyond the Spectacle: Native North American Presence in Britain
Description: Prof. David Stirrup hosts an opportunity to learn about contemporary Indigenous issues in Canada and the USA. An exhibition of posters highlights the topics, from anti-pipeline protests to cultural appropriation, alongside Scotland’s long historical ties with Indigenous communities, from WWI soldiers to Cherokee Chiefs. Native North American speakers will join academics from the Beyond the Spectacle project and Scottish universities to answer questions inspired by the exhibit. Suitable for all ages and all levels of interest and prior knowledge.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: The Tempest & The Teller
Description: Shakespeare’s The Tempest is brought to life by storyteller Alexander Mackenzie. Hold on to your seats for a telling infused with ribald imagination from beginning to end, told in a language that is free, bold and poised between imagination and ancient plot. The Tempest and The Teller weaves together the old and the new, ignited by Alexander’s illustrations that colourfully depict the exciting twists and turns of this most allegorical of tales.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Scotland & Canada: Stories from Orkney & Quebec
Description: After sharing stories at the ceilidhs of the recently finished Orkney Storytelling Festival, Quebecoise Metis Mi’kmaq and Acadian Robert Seven Crows Bourdon and Orcadian Tom Muir have even more stories to tell! Come and join them in this unique event where they will take you from coast to coast.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Stories I’ve Lived In (Cancelled)
Description:
Salish storyteller Julie Cajune shares stories that have shaped her identity as an American woman. These accounts portray the lived experience of her female family descendants from Salish, Nez Perce, Anishinaabe and Scots ancestry. They span shame and pride, fear and forgiveness, exploring the frailties and strengths of our human condition, with the stories enhanced by talented musicians Hector MacInnes and Leighton Jones.
   *Due to unforeseen circumstances, this event has been cancelled - we apologise for any inconvenience*
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Masterclass: Exploring Contemporary Coastal Dance
Description:
British Columbia’s Dancers of Damelahamid facilitate a movement-based workshop centred on contemporary Coastal Indigenous dance form, allowing participants to enjoy the shared experience of dance. Discover the dynamic and innovative qualities of Indigenous practices with dance instruction, exploratory work and partnered improvisation.
 All levels of dance experience welcome, however the workshop is most catered to those with a dance background. Please dress comfortably and wear moccasins, dance shoes, or bare feet.
 Please note this workshop is taking place at Dance Base , 14-16 Grassmarket, Edinburgh, EH1 2JU

Title: Airts o Soons an Een: Scotland’s Art in Scots
Description:
Theatre artist and Scots language advocate Ishbel McFarlane explores the cultural importance of Scots – also called Doric, Glaswegian and Lallans amongst others – through key pieces in the National Galleries of Scotland in an illuminating talk, which highlights how linguistic culture interacts with visual culture.
 Event held at Scottish National Portrait Gallery.

Title: Stories of the Fianna in a Modern World / Sgeulachdan na Fèinne san Latha an-diugh
Description:
How can we be faithful to our heritage while engaging with modern Gaels, in terms of context, style and vocabulary? Ruairidh Maclean presents some old stories that belong to Scotland’s Gaelic tradition and highlights how they still resonate today.
 Please note this workshop is in Gaelic. Ciamar as urrainn dhuinn a bhith dìleas ri ar dualchas agus aig an aon àm a bhith untainneach ri Gàidheil an latha an-diugh a thaobh modh is cainnt? Bheir sinn sùil air seann sgeulachdan à dualchas Gàidheil na h-Alba agus mar as urrainn tlachd is toileachas fhaighinn bhuapa fhathast, le Ruairidh MacIlleathain. Bidh a’ bhùth-obrach air fad ann an Gàidhlig.

Title: The Very Curious Herbal
Description:
Storyteller Amanda Edmiston embarks on an enchanted journey into the verdant world of the 18th century. Inspired by Elizabeth Blackwell’s ‘A Curious Herbal’, the first book of its kind created by a woman and published, this multidimensional performance layers history, stories, tastes and remedies to draw us into the garden of plants revealed within the book.
 Tickets for National Library of Scotland events are available on eventbrite or 0131 623 3734. Book Your Ticket
Venue address: National Library of Scotland, George IV Bridge, Edinburgh

Title: Stories Old and New Through Our Songs / Sgeulachdan seana is ùra tror n-òrain
Description:
Inverness-based duo Brian Ó hEadhra and Fiona Mackenzie perform traditional and contemporary songs in Gaelic and English that explore culture and tales from the Highlands, past and present. In this special SISF show, the duo will read some translations of the ancient and new Gaelic verse before singing in their distinctive style and harmonies. Not to be missed!
 Gaelic song translations available.
 Bidh na seinneadairean Brian Ó hEadhra agus Fiona NicChoinnich a’ gabhail òrain seana is ùra às a’ Ghàidhealtachd ann an Gàidhlig is ann am Beurla. Mar phàirt dhan chonsairt sònraichte seo, bidh iad cuideachd a’ leughadh eadar-theangaichean dhan bhàrdachd Ghàidhlig. Oidhche sònraichte a bhios ann!
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Flicker
Description: As the festival approaches its finale, the British Columbian Dancers of Damelahamid showcase a second night of ancient dances and songs that highlight the complexities of contemporary Indigenous identities. Just as light shimmers, Flicker represents the moments through which one can cross space and time, as the masked dancers’ journey in and out of the spirit world of their ancestors.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Samhuinn Fire Festival
Description:
The Beltane Fire Society celebrates the Celtic New Year by marking the end of summer and welcoming the onset of winter with a stunning torch-lit procession featuring acrobatics, fireworks, beautiful costumes and breathtaking performances.
 Tickets available at www.beltane.org

Title: Evening Twilight / Ciaradh na h-Oidhche
Description:
Pàdruig Morrison, Linda MacLeod, Seonaidh MacIntyre, Shona Masson and Calum MacDonald recreate a vital setting for the transmission of stories, songs, tunes and lore in the Gàidhealtachd (the ceilidh-house). The quintet are inheritors of the language and culture of Uist and Skye, who combine to share and celebrate the old tradition we are in risk of losing. The evening will be a fully Gaelic production, led by young Gaels who pursue busy lives promoting Gaelic culture and arts with vigour and passion.
 Performance in Gaelic, with summary translation programmes.
 Tha Pàdruig Moireasdan, Linda NicLeòid, Seonaidh Mac an t-Saoir, Shona Masson and Calum Dòmhnallach a’ toirt sealladh den taigh-cèilidh, mu dh’fhaoide an t-àit’ is cudromaiche gus sgeulachdan, òrain, puirt agus seanchas nan Gàidheal a chumail beò thar na linntean. Mar chòignear a tha nan oighrean air cànan is cultar Uibhist agus an t-Eilean Sgitheanach, agus nan cuid-obrach mar luchd-brosnachaidh cultar na Gàidhlig, ann an Ciaradh na h-Oidhche tha iad a’ toirt sgairt is beatha dhan t-seann traidisean.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Code: Torchlight Procession in partnership with Visit Scotland
Title: Torchlight Procession in partnership with Visit Scotland
Description:
BE a trailblazer

Blaze through the city accompanied by pipers and drummers, fire and fanfare and forge a river of light through the heart of Edinburgh’s Old Town. A spectacular and unforgettable family friendly event culminating in the historic Holyrood Park.

On reaching the park, you will come together with your fellow torchbearers to form an image of two people shaking hands, which will be captured from the air and broadcast around the world!

You must have a ticket to take part in the Torchlight Procession in partnership with VisitScotland.

50p from every ticket bought goes to OneCity Trust, fighting inequality and exclusion in the City of Edinburgh.
Venue description: The procession has three starting points. Your starting point will be clearly marked on your tickets (Zone 1 = St Giles' Street, Zone 2 = North Bridge, Zone 3 = South Bridge). You must pick your starting point when you purchase your ticket and you will not be able to change it later. You will only be able to enter and collect your torch at your chosen starting point.

Title: Ceilidh under the Castle
Description:
BE iconic

Start the New Year the Scottish way at the Ceilidh under the Castle.

Whirl or jig, fling or be flung under the watchful eye of Edinburgh Castle. Join hands with old friends and new to dance in the New Year with a full ceilidh band and plenty of local food and drink to keep you spinning all night.

This year’s jigs and reels will be brought to you by three smashing ceilidh bands: Sleekit Beasties, Skyte! and Cool Ceol Ceilidh Band.

At midnight, welcome in 2020 with a breath taking fireworks display, amidst the historic setting of the majestic Edinburgh Castle.
Venue description:
Arena open from 7.30pm.
Enter via Lothian Road onto King’s Stables Road and through the grounds of St Cuthbert’s Parish Church.
Whilst there are no age restrictions and children are welcome, we do not recommend this event for very young children and strictly no buggies permitted. Not recommended for babes in arms.
No entry to the arena after 10.30pm. So please come early!

Title: Bairns Afore
Description:
BE with your clan

Enjoy the Edinburgh’s Hogmanay experience as a family and still have the kids tucked up in bed afore the bells at Bairns Afore, the best family gig imaginable.

Join legendary comic duo and heroes of children’s TV, Dick and Dom, as they battle it out behind the decks to see whose tunes are the best!

The gig is topped off by its very own spectacular ‘midnight’ fireworks moment, allowing families to take their children home to bed before the late-night revelling gets underway.
Venue description:
Doors open at 4.00pm.
All children must be accompanied by an adult at all times.
Strictly no buggies within the enclosure area, but buggy parking is available.
Children under 2 years of age do not require a ticket.

Title: Symphonic Ibiza
Description:
BE ready to party

Featuring some of the most famous Ibiza club anthems from the last 30 years, celebrate the European island of clubbing in the magnificent surroundings of the historic McEwan Hall.

Symphonic Ibiza fuses the thrilling live Orchestra with high tempo beats from renowned club DJ Andy Joyce and musical genius Steve Etherington, whose credentials include residencies at Ibiza super-clubs Pacha, Amnesia, Eden and Café Mambo, this party is like no other, creating an entirely new club experience.

★★★★★ ‘Absolutely brilliant night out.’ One4Review

★★★★★ ‘It is a party like no other, a totally unique experience and massive night out’  The Scottish Sun
Venue description:
Doors open at 8.00pm.
There is an interval during this performance.
This event is not recommended for children under 12 years old.
Anyone under 16 years old must be accompanied by an adult over 21 years of age at all times.

Code: Ronnie Scott’s Big Band in Concert
Title: Ronnie Scott’s Big Band in Concert
Description:
BE brassy

Direct from London’s world-famous jazz club, Ronnie Scott’s Big Band is ready to swing you into 2020 in the magnificent surroundings of the historic McEwan Hall.

Playing their iconic blend of jazz, blues and swing, with acclaimed jazz singer and pianist Liane Carroll taking centre stage, get ready for a rousing and unforgettable finale to 2019 from the greatest musicians the UK has to offer!

This event takes place in McEwan Hall, your ticket also includes access to the Street Party hosted by Johnnie Walker. The event will finish at 10pm and access to the Street Party is available until 10:30pm, McEwan Hall to the Bank Street entrance to the Street Party is approximately an 8 minute walk.
Venue description:
Doors open at 6.30pm
There is an interval during this performance.
This event is not recommended for children under 12 years old.
This is a fully seated event in McEwan Hall.
Anyone under 16 years old must be accompanied by an adult over 21 years of age at all times.

Title: G’day 2020 with Kylie Auldist
Description:
BE global

Grab your mates and kickstart your New Year with the rest of the Southern Hemisphere at our brand new Australian New Year party with Kylie Auldist, ‘the high priestess of Melbourne soul’ (The Music Magazine) and leading lady of Australian funk & soul stalwarts, The Bamboos.

When the clock strikes midnight in Sydney embrace your Neighbours (who might become good friends) and get ready for an absolute ripper of a party, complete with plenty of classic Aussie tunes, Bondi Beach vibes and even a few tinnies. A little slice of Home (for our Australian pals) and Away (for everyone else) this Hogmanay.
Venue description:
Doors open at 11.00am.
Anyone under 16 years old must be accompanied by an adult over 21 years of age at all times.

Title: First Footers Family Ceilidh
Description:
BE a tiny dancer

Come one, come all, to the first ceilidh of 2020 in the magnificent McEwan Hall!

Gather your nearest and dearest to reel, jig, two-step and waltz those Hogmanay cobwebs away at our family-friendly, completely free event.

Tickets are free but must be booked in advance.
Venue description:
Doors open at 11.30am
Tickets are per person.
All children must be accompanied by an adult at all times.
Children under 2 years of age do not require a ticket.

Title: Edinburgh’s Hogmanay Official After-Party
Description:
BE out all night

Not ready for your Hogmanay to end? Neither are we!

Keep those celebrations going with a host of the top DJs, including a late-night set from the one and only Judge Jules, as we kickstart 2020 in style at McEwan Hall. A truly epic after party you won’t want to miss out on.
Venue description:
Doors open at 1.00am.
This event is over 18s only.

Title: Loony Dook
Description:
BE daring

The Loony Dook continues its New Year’s Day tradition at South Queensferry. In the shadow of the Forth Bridges, the dippers in fancy dress, scantily clad or even fully clothed from the night before will brave the chill to raise money for charities while shaking off their Hogmanay hangover.

Dookers will march the length of South Queensferry High Street as part of the Dookers’ Parade before launching themselves into the freezing Firth of Forth.

Spectators are welcome to cheer on the Dookers at various vantage points along the route or down on the beach.

South Queensferry has a variety of pubs, cafes and restaurants, all open on New Year’s Day.

Title: Candlelit Concert
Description:
BE festive

A festive end of year celebration in the candlelit atmosphere of St Giles' Cathedral.

This year’s concert celebrates Christmas and the New Year with the first and last cantatas from J.S.Bach’s Christmas Oratorio taking centre stage in the programme featuring Bach at his most exuberant.  The Baroque theme continues with Antonio Vivaldi’s sparkling setting of Dixit Dominus.

St Giles' Cathedral Choir, directed by Michael Harris, with the St Giles' Camerata, leader Angus Ramsay, are joined by a stunning array of talented young soloists.

Title: Eddi Reader
Description:
BE enthralled

Celebrating 40 years as a live performer, Eddi Reader has effortlessly developed into one of popular music’s most thrilling and affecting performers.

With 9 critically acclaimed solo albums and 3 BRIT awards to her name, join Eddi for an evening of music spanning her prestigious career of pop, folk and jazz.
Venue description:
Doors open at 5.00pm.
Anyone under 16 years must be accompanied by an adult over 21 years of age.

Title: Message from the Skies
Description:
BE inspired

Message from the Skies returns to Edinburgh’s Hogmanay on 1 January with Shorelines, a collection of letters to Scotland reflecting on our relationship with our seas, waters and coasts and our maritime heritage.

The words of five celebrated writers: Charlotte Runcie, Irvine Welsh, Kathleen Jamie, Kayus Bankole and Robin Robinson – will illuminate and animate landmarks around the city with a maritime theme this January.

Message from the Skies: Shorelines runs from 1-25 January 2020 and is developed in partnership with Edinburgh City of Literature and the Edinburgh International Book Festival and funded by Creative Scotland through the Scottish Government’s Festivals EXPO fund.

Projection locations will be announced in December 2019. 

From 01.01.20, download the Messages from the Skies app to read or listen to the stories and to get directions to projection locations.
Venue description:
The projections will run daily from 1 to 25 January, from dusk 5pm until 10pm.  
As this is an outdoor walking event in winter, please dress comfortably and for the weather.

Title: Scotland & Canada: My Home Canada & My Home-Home Scotland
Description: When you emigrate where is your home? Where do your stories take you? Can you ever ‘Go back where you came from’? And why would you want to? Storyteller Alexandria Patience tells stories of her homes, Scotland and Canada.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: The Travel Journal (Sold Out)
Description:
A hands-on workshop with illustrator Kim Howard incorporating collage, writing, maps, drawing and painting to create a handmade, personalised sketch diary. Materials will be provided, but attendees may bring their own personal collage items. Exercises are fun, quick and satisfying with no drawing skill necessary to a complete your book.
 *Please note this event is now sold out.*

Title: Scotland & Canada: Robert Service – Poet of the Yukon
Description: Storytellers David Campbell, Barbara McLean and cellist/singer Wendy Weatherby celebrate poet and writer Robert W. Service. Discover his early life in Scotland and meteoric rise to fame with stirring verses of the outback, goldrush characters and wild adventurers, including the iconic Dan McGrew and Sam Magee.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Scotland & Canada – Mutual Relations
Description:
Explore the close historical and cultural connections between Canada and Scotland, and their continuing legacy. Chief RoseAnne Archibald is a First Nation activist and educator with family ties to Scotland. Donald Smith reflects on the sometimes-troubled relationship between Scots and First Nation peoples through the novels ‘River Thieves’ by Michael Crummey and ‘Sick Heart River’ by John Buchan.
 Tickets for National Library of Scotland events are available on eventbrite or 0131 623 3734. Book Your Ticket
Venue address: National Library of Scotland, George IV Bridge, Edinburgh

Title: In Conversation with Gary Green
Description: Discover the fascinating backgrounds of our guests with insights from Scottish-based hosts. Newfoundland and Labrador storyteller Gary Green is welcomed by storyteller Donald Smith.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Words on the Street
Description:
Street games, stories and songs for all the family! Take part in the vibrant children’s games and surreal songs of old Edinburgh and explore the story of the local street outside. Featuring an array of Scottish storytellers and sessions for all ages.
 Programme Storytelling Court & Outside All Ages | 1.30pm – 4pm Macastory lead a variety of pop-up stories and songs, performances and games throughout the afternoon. Museum of Childhood Ages 4+ | 1.30pm – 4pm 20 minute storytelling sessions on the hour and half hour. Scottish Storytelling Centre Library (1st floor) Ages 4+ | 1.30pm – 4pm 20 minute storytelling sessions on the hour and half hour. Edinburgh's Literary Quarter Walking Tours (start at John Knox House) Adults and children 8+ | All day Be inspired by Edinburgh’s literary past, present and future, with a self-guided walking tour exploring Edinburgh’s Literary Quarter. The Museum of Childhood is situated directly across the road from the Storytelling Centre.
Venue: Scottish Storytelling Centre & Museum of Childhood
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, 43-45 High St, Edinburgh

Title: Human Library
Description: This library works just like a normal library: visitors browse the catalogue, choose the book they want to read and borrow it. But in the Human Library, books are people, and reading consists of conversation! The Human Library seeks to challenge prejudice and discrimination in a warm, inclusive and welcoming space. This event is organised by Laura Pasternak, a young Regional Ambassador for the Holocaust Educational Trust in collaboration with the Scottish International Storytelling Festival. In association with The Human Library Organisation. Visit https://humanlibrary.org/ for more information. Drop-in throughout the day!
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Life with My Father, George Orwell (Sold Out)
Description:
George Orwell’s son Richard Blair takes us on a personal and unique journey into the life of his father, including insights into family times on the Isle of Jura.
   *Please note this event is now sold out.*
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Global Lab – Day 1: Politics of Folktales
Description:
An opportunity to discover the power of storytelling and role of storytellers in the 21st century. Each day features keynote stories, talks, discussions and workshops in open sessions, allowing for shared reflection ahead of the evening’s storytelling performances.
 Are folktales still subversive, fantastic and anarchic, or mainly entertainment? Are they told for more personal, family or social issues? How do you read an audience and draw out interpretations that they can develop in heart, mind and action? Learn from the approaches of accomplished tellers Jan Blake, Heidi Dahlsveen and Ruth Kirkpatrick.
 Lunch included in ticket price. Full Programme
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Global Lab – Day 2: Earth Stories
Description:
An opportunity to discover the power of storytelling and role of storytellers in the 21st century. Each day features keynote stories, talks, discussions and workshops in open sessions, allowing for shared reflection ahead of the evening’s storytelling performances.
 As our global crisis deepens, which stories can help us reconnect and provoke real change? Can the stories of indigenous people be restored to a place of honour and inspiration for all? Contributions from Alette Willis, Grian Cutanda, Dawne McFarlane, Chief RoseAnne Archibald and Anamaria Lines.
 Lunch included in ticket price. Full Programme
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Global Lab – Day 4: Talking Cures
Description:
An opportunity to discover the power of storytelling and role of storytellers in the 21st century. Each day features keynote stories, talks, discussions and workshops in open sessions, allowing for shared reflection ahead of the evening’s storytelling performances.
 It’s good to talk – internationally, nationally, within communities and families. How can storytelling enable understanding that goes ‘Beyond Words’? This special ‘Year of Conversation’ workshop is held on United Nations Day. Contributions from Michael Williams, Amanda Edmiston, Tom Pow, Ailie Finlay and Edel Roddy.
 Lunch included in ticket price. Full Programme
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Global Lab – Day 5: Transforming Myth
Description:
An opportunity to discover the power of storytelling and role of storytellers in the 21st century. Each day features keynote stories, talks, discussions and workshops in open sessions, allowing for shared reflection ahead of the evening’s storytelling performances.
 Myths are one of the richest emotional and intellectual human cultural expressions. They explore our place in nature, our relationships and spirituality. How do artists express that narrative inheritance in their art and why? Experience different traditions and diverse ways of expressing them. Contributions from Margaret Grenier, George Macpherson, Giovanna Conforto and Grian Cutanda.
 Lunch included in ticket price. Full Programme
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Global Lab – Day 3: The Wild Nature & Garden Cosmos
Description:
An opportunity to discover the power of storytelling and role of storytellers in the 21st century. Each day features keynote stories, talks, discussions and workshops in open sessions, allowing for shared reflection ahead of the evening’s storytelling performances.
 How do traditional and contemporary stories take us into a shared experience of ‘the wild’? Are gardens a place where humanity and the natural world converse and commune? How can storytellers channel these experiences and open doors in tactful and inviting ways? Contributions from Donald Smith, Margot Henderson, Joanna Geyer-Kordesch and Giovanna Conforto.
 Full Programme Please note this event is taking place at the Botanic Cottage, Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. Lunch not included, but catering options on site. *Tickets only now available on the day by calling the Storytelling Centre Box Office on 0131 556 9579*
Venue address: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, Arboretum Place, Edinburgh

Title: The Devil & the Clutch of Fools
Description:
The culmination of SISF is for you to join in with a story… whoever you are! Experienced bards or complete novices, young or old, grimy or beautiful, we all go into Hallowe’en with a certain sense of foreboding. It is a time when the veil between light and dark invites the unholy to be blessed and the innocent to be drowned. This marathon event brings storytellers from different nations together with local people in a storytelling extravaganza, to face off against the demons of Hallowe’en, with a special improvised ceilidh telling of ‘Tam O’ Shanter’ to fire the imagination around 8pm. Come along if you dare. Hosted by the irrepressible storyteller Alexander Mackenzie.
 To book a storytelling slot please contact Alexander Mackenzie alexander.george.mackenzie@gmail.com or 07976221179
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Greyfriars Bobby & his Four-Legged Friends: Amazing Edinburgh Animals! (Sold Out)
Description:
Join Fergus McNicol and his tour guide Chloe the Cockapoo for a storytelling tour of amazing Edinburgh animal tales! We know about Greyfriars Bobby, but why is there a (cheeky) monkey on the High Street, an elephant in the Castle and a bear in the Gardens? Enjoy the trail and discover the answers, with story, song and dance along the way!
   Meet at Greyfriars Kirkyard, next to the Art Shop.   *Please note, this event has now sold out*

Title: Open Hearth – New Moon
Description: Storytellers and musicians gather round the hearth for a relaxed traditional session of stories from home and abroad, as the darkness closes in and minds glow with pictures in the symbolic fire. The perfect way to end your day! Hosted by Marie Louise Cochrane, with guest storytellers Giovanna Conforto from Italy, Margaret Grenier from Canada, Linda Williamson, Mio Shudo and Claire Hewitt.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: 365: Stories and Music
Description:
A sound installation of contemporary Scottish stories and music by author James Robertson and musician Aidan O’Rourke.
 Bold, tender, full of old truths and distilled modern wit, this is an epic built on the beauty of the miniature. A collaboration between artists steeped in tradition but constantly breaking new ground.
 James Robertson, one of Scotland’s most respected authors, wrote a short story every day for a year. Each story was to be 365 words, no more, no less. It became an enchanting, roaming collection of fairytales, memories and provocations published in 2014 as 365:Stories. That was only the beginning. Fiddler/composer Aidan O’Rourke (of the folk supertrio Lau) wrote a tune every day in response, resulting in a major new body of 365 tunes. The installation is a piece of art in itself, beautifully crafted from oak and steel with no digital screens in sight. It allows up to six people at a time to browse through all 365 stories and listen through headphones. Each spoken word-recording is paired with a piece of music. Robertson reads many himself; other storytellers include Tam Dean Burn, Gerda Stevenson, Cathy Macdonald, Matthew Zajac and Kate Molleson providing rich and varied accents from around Scotland. The exhibition space is occasionally closed for private functions. Please call 0131 556 9579 to check.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Drawing the Story
Description:
Illustrator Kim Howard creates real time sketches and drawings of performers, participants and audiences during the SISF, capturing moments of engagement and the connections made between people, place and story.
 Kim will also be leading the Travel Journal workshop on Sat 26 October. The exhibition space is occasionally closed for private functions. Please call 0131 556 9579 to check.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: The Somewhere Else
Description:
Glasgow-based artist Fiona Watson spent her childhood in Canada thanks to wandering Scottish parents. Her romanticised memories are of icebergs floating into St. John’s harbour and skating on the frozen waters of Ontario, surrounded by wild nature. In this series of etching prints, the artist expresses her overwhelming visual memory of Canada, evoking the silence and minimalist aesthetic of its snowy landscapes.
 Exhibition runs Sat 5 - Thu 31 Oct. The exhibition is also available to view before evening events, however the exhibition space is occasionally closed for private functions. Please call 0131 556 9579 to check availability.
Venue address: Scottish Storytelling Centre, High Street, Edinburgh, United Kingdom

Title: Northern Lights: The Scottish Enlightenment
Description:
18th-century Scotland was a place with many remarkable individuals, but the conditions that helped create the Scottish Enlightenment were the social and professional networks that allowed these great thinkers to share and develop their ideas. Intellectual Scots in the 18th century lived active and sociable lives with frequent opportunities to debate with their peers: from universities, churches, debating societies, libraries and laboratories to coffee shops, taverns and town houses. Featuring books and manuscripts produced by the leading figures of the age including David Hume, Adam Smith, William Robertson, Robert Adam and Robert Burns.
 Exhibition runs 21 Jun 2019 – 18 Apr 2020.
 Open: Mon, Tue, Thu: 9.30am – 7pm | Wed: 10am – 7pm | Fri & Sat: 9.30am – 5pm
 Free entry.
Venue address: National Library of Scotland, George IV Bridge, Edinburgh

Title: Hamish Henderson (1919 – 2002)
Description:
A display celebrating the life and work of poet, songwriter, and folklorist Hamish Henderson, drawn from the collections at the National Library of Scotland.
 Exhibition runs 23 Sep - 12 Nov 2019.
 Open: Mon, Tue, Thu: 9.30am – 7pm | Wed: 10am – 7pm | Fri & Sat: 9.30am – 5pm
 Free entry.
Venue address: National Library of Scotland, George IV Bridge, Edinburgh

There is no greater pleasure than the power of traditional storytelling, taking listeners on a journey of the imagination. Code: Mark Ronson’s Hogmanay in the Gardens
Title: Mark Ronson’s Hogmanay in the Gardens
Description:
BE blown away

Celebrate Hogmanay in spectacular style with Grammy and Oscar Award winner Mark Ronson, Rudimental DJ and Mungo's Hi Fi.

Join one of the biggest names in the music industry at Edinburgh’s Hogmanay’s for the party of a lifetime. He’s worked with pop royalty, from Stevie Wonder to Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars and now Mark Ronson will play ALL-THE-HITS to thousands of party-goers at Edinburgh’s Hogmanay.

This year Mark Ronson is joined by special guest global chart-topper Rudimental DJ, bringing a back catelogue of massive hits!

Title: Night Walk for Edinburgh
Description:
BE intrigued

Janet Cardiff and George Bures Miller's critically acclaimed Night Walk for Edinburgh returns.

Pick up a screen and a pair of headphones and set off for an hour's adventure with the artist's voice in your ears and magical scenes unfolding on a screen in your hand. Part game-playing, part surrealistic poetry, even murder mystery, the Night Walk is layered with history, invention and memories.

Free Event

3.30PM - 5PM slots available every 15 minutes

Commissioned for the city of Edinburgh by The Fruitmarket Gallery and presented in partnership with Edinburgh’s Christmas and Hogmanay.
Venue address:
Start at Bookmarket
Waverley Mall
Edinburgh
Venue description:
Following Janet Cardiff’s voice and walking in her footsteps, you will be led through the backstreets of the Edinburgh’s Old Town, unravelling a disjointed tale – part game-playing, part surrealistic poetry, perhaps even a murder mystery – layered with history, invention and memories.

Night Walk for Edinburgh involves c.120 steps up and 30 down, and uneven ground. Please dress for the terrain and the weather. For those who need it, we are pleased to offer a seated version, inside at Bookmarket, running daily at 3.45 and 4.45pm.
